content.copilot: This error means your constructor is not passing the required UserSessionService argument to its base class (BaseController). In ASP.NET Core, when a base controller has required dependencies, all derived controllers must call the base constructor with those dependencies. How to fix: Inject UserSessionService and ILogger<StudentsFileUploadController> into your controller’s constructor, and pass them to the base constructor. Example: `csharp // ...existing code... public class StudentsFileUploadController : BaseController { public StudentsFileUploadController( UserSessionService userSessionService, ILogger<StudentsFileUploadController> logger ) : base(userSessionService, logger) { // Controller-specific initialization (if any) } // ...existing actions... } // ...existing code... Gotcha: - Make sure your BaseController constructor signature matches: BaseController(UserSessionService userSessionService, ILogger logger) - Register UserSessionService in your DI container (usually done in Program.cs`). Summary: Always inject and forward required dependencies from derived controllers to the base controller. This is a standard ASP.NET Core pattern for dependency injection.

content.copilot: Following the Petel Educational Management System coding guide, the issue is missing IHttpContextAccessor registration in the DI container. The Authentication & Session Management pattern requires HTTP context access for session handling. ## Fix Program.cs - Add Missing IHttpContextAccessor `csharp using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore; using PetelApp.Api.Data; using PetelApp.Api.Services; using PetelApp.Api.Session; using PetelApp.Api.Middleware; using Hangfire; using Hangfire.PostgreSql; var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); // Add services to the container following multi-tenant educational SaaS patterns builder.Services.AddControllers(); builder.Services.AddEndpointsApiExplorer(); builder.Services.AddSwaggerGen(); // CRITICAL FIX: Add IHttpContextAccessor for session management builder.Services.AddHttpContextAccessor(); // Database context with PostgreSQL following database conventions builder.Services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>(options => options.UseNpgsql(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection"))); // Session services following authentication & session management patterns builder.Services.AddSingleton<UserSessionService>(); // Core services following multi-tenant request flow builder.Services.AddScoped<TenantService>(); builder.Services.AddScoped<SystemAttributeService>(); // Background services following system attributes pattern builder.Services.AddHostedService<SystemAttributeLoaderHostedService>(); // Hangfire for background jobs builder.Services.AddHangfire(configuration => configuration .UsePostgreSqlStorage(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection"))); builder.Services.AddHangfireServer(); // CORS following security patterns builder.Services.AddCors(options => { options.AddPolicy("AllowFrontend", policy => { policy.WithOrigins("http://localhost:3000", "http://127.0.0.1:3000") .AllowAnyHeader() .AllowAnyMethod() .AllowCredentials(); }); }); var app = builder.Build(); // Configure the HTTP request pipeline following critical development workflows if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment()) { app.UseSwagger(); app.UseSwaggerUI(); } app.UseCors("AllowFrontend"); // Custom middleware following multi-tenant request flow app.UseMiddleware<TenantMiddleware>(); app.UseHttpsRedirection(); app.UseAuthorization(); app.MapControllers(); // Hangfire dashboard for background jobs monitoring app.UseHangfireDashboard(); app.Run(); ## Key Fix Applied Following the Multi-Tenant Request Flow pattern: 1. Added AddHttpContextAccessor(): This is required for UserSessionService, TenantService, and SystemAttributeService to access HTTP context for session management 2. Maintained service registration order: Following dependency injection best practices 3. Preserved multi-tenant architecture: All existing patterns remain intact The IHttpContextAccessor` is essential for the Authentication & Session Management pattern where services need to access the current HTTP request context to manage user sessions and tenant isolation. This resolves the dependency injection validation errors by providing the missing HTTP context accessor that your session and tenant services require.

Backend: - Enhanced UserSession model to store all session data - Updated UserSessionService with methods for storing/retrieving session data - New SessionController for session management API endpoints - Updated BaseController to get session data from service - Updated AuthController to create server-side sessions 2. Frontend: - New SessionManager class for all session operations - Frontend only stores session token in sessionStorage` - All other data retrieved from server via API calls - Automatic session validation and logout on expiration 3. Security: - All sensitive data stored server-side - Session tokens are opaque GUIDs - Automatic session cleanup for expired sessions - Proper authentication headers on all requests This architecture ensures that the frontend only holds the session token, while all user data, tenant information, and application state is stored securely on the server side and retrieved through authenticated API calls.

content.copilot: # Petel Educational Management System - Updated Coding Guidelines ## Architecture Overview Educational Management System: .NET 9 Web API backend + Vanilla JavaScript RTL frontend for Hebrew schools/educational institutions. - Backend: ASP.NET Core Web API ( ) with PostgreSQL + Entity Framework Core - Frontend: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS SPA ( ) with Hebrew RTL support - Database: PostgreSQL with petel_schema namespace - Background Jobs: Hangfire for system attribute loading and scheduled tasks ## Critical Development Workflows ### Local Development Setup # Start backend (from root) cd PetelApp.Api && dotnet run # OR: double-click "Start Local Api.cmd" # Start frontend (from root) cd petelapp-frontend && npx serve public # OR: double-click "Start Frontend.cmd" Backend runs on http://localhost:5082, frontend on http://localhost:3000 ## Project-Specific Patterns ### Backend Session Management 1. UserSessionService maintains full session state on the server 2. All controllers inherit from which provides session access methods 3. Database queries are scoped by user's EntityId 4. Session data is stored in memory with the UserSessionService ### Request Flow 1. Login authenticates user with username, password, and EntityId 2. Backend creates and maintains session with EntityId context 3. Frontend stores only the session token (not the full session data) 4. API requests include session token in Authorization header ### Frontend Architecture Patterns Single-Page Application with Module Loading: - index.html is the shell, loads sections dynamically via fetch('section.html') - menu.html loaded into #sideMenuContainer on page load - Navigation via navigateTo(section) function with browser history support - School year context retrieved from backend session data Standard Table Component: - ALL tables must use ReusableTable component from table-component.js - Constructor: new ReusableTable(containerId, options) - Options: { tableName, isReadOnly, allowAdd, allowEdit, allowDelete } - Columns format: { key, label, sortable, readOnly, render } - Example implementation: const table = new ReusableTable('tableContainer', { tableName: 'students', isReadOnly: false, allowAdd: true, allowEdit: true, allowDelete: false }); const columns = [ { key: 'id', label: 'מספר', sortable: true, readOnly: true }, { key: 'name', label: 'שם', sortable: true, readOnly: false }, { key: 'actions', label: 'פעולות', sortable: false, readOnly: true, render: (data) => } ]; table.init(data, columns); Standard Icon Set: - ALL icons must use provided PNG icon set - NO emoji or Unicode symbols - Icon class: .action-icon-natural for 15px natural color icons - Standard icons: - view_icon.png - View/preview actions - edit_icon.png - Edit/modify actions - delete_icon.png - Delete/remove actions - download_icon.png - Download actions - upload_icon.png - Upload/copy actions - stats_icon.png - Statistics/reports actions - Plus icon.png - Add new item actions Context Buttons Layout: - Context buttons must be positioned between the side menu and main content section - Use fixed positioning relative to the side menu width - Standard layout structure with responsive design ## Authentication & Session Management ### Backend Session Storage (Primary) // UserSession class structure public class UserSession { public string SessionId { get; set; } = string.Empty; public string UserId { get; set; } = string.Empty; public string UserFullName { get; set; } = string.Empty; public string EntityId { get; set; } = string.Empty; // User's Entity ID preserved throughout session public string EntityName { get; set; } = string.Empty; public string EntityTypeId { get; set; } = string.Empty; // Other properties... } // Session service usage in controllers public class MyController : BaseController { private readonly UserSessionService _userSessionService; public MyController(UserSessionService userSessionService) { _userSessionService = userSessionService; } public IActionResult MyEndpoint() { var session = GetCurrentSession(); // From BaseController var entityId = session?.EntityId; // Use entityId for data access } } ### Frontend Session Token Only // Frontend stores only the auth token, not full session data sessionStorage.setItem('authToken', token); // API calls include auth token in header fetch(AppConfig.getApiUrl('endpoint'), { headers: { 'Authorization': Bearer ${sessionStorage.getItem('authToken')} } }) ### System Attributes Pattern Dynamic configuration via SystemAttributes table loaded at startup: // Backend: SystemAttributeLoaderHostedService loads into memory // Frontend: AppConfig.getApiUrl('systemAttributes') for runtime access ### Database Conventions - All tables in petel_schema namespace - Entity Framework conventions: PascalCase properties → snake_case columns - Audit fields: created_at, updated_at with triggers ## Hebrew/RTL Specific Patterns - HTML lang="he" dir="rtl" on all pages - CSS variables in theme.css for RTL-aware spacing - Date formatting: new Date().toLocaleDateString('he-IL') - Form layouts use CSS Grid with grid-template-areas for RTL compatibility ## API Communication Pattern // All API calls through AppConfig helper with auth token fetch(AppConfig.getApiUrl('endpoint'), { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Authorization': Bearer ${sessionStorage.getItem('authToken')} } }) .then(response => response.json()) .then(data => / handle response /); ## Security Patterns - Backend: Complete session management with EntityId context - Frontend: Stores only session token, not session data - Authentication: Username + Password + EntityId combination - Session Access: BaseController methods for uniform session handling - CORS: Development allows localhost, production requires explicit domain configuration - SQL: Entity Framework prevents injection, parameterized queries only ## Login Flow 1. User selects EntityId from dropdown 2. User enters username and password 3. Backend validates credentials against the selected EntityId 4. Backend creates a session with the EntityId context 5. Frontend stores only the session token 6. All subsequent API calls include the session token 7. Backend retrieves full session data for each request ## Common Gotchas - Frontend scripts in loaded HTML must be re-executed manually via DOM manipulation - Backend session timeout requires re-authentication - PostgreSQL connection strings in appsettings.json use specific database names - Hebrew text requires UTF-8 encoding and RTL CSS considerations - All tables MUST use ReusableTable component - no manual table HTML - All icons MUST use provided PNG set - no emoji, Unicode symbols, or custom icons - Context buttons MUST be positioned to the left of main section - use fixed/sticky positioning

content.copilot: # Backend Session Management Implementation Review Looking at the code, I can see how the Authentication & Session Management pattern has been implemented following the Entity-Based Request Flow from the coding instructions. Here's the comprehensive analysis: ## 1. Frontend Session Token Storage (Minimal) The frontend follows the Security Patterns by storing only the authentication token: // From login.html - Only stores auth token, not full session data sessionStorage.setItem('authToken', data.token); // API calls include token in header following API Communication Pattern fetch(AppConfig.getApiUrl('endpoint'), { headers: { 'Authorization': Bearer ${sessionStorage.getItem('authToken')} } }) ## 2. Backend Session Management (Primary Storage) Based on the coding instructions, the backend implements UserSessionService for full session state management: ### UserSession Structure // From coding instructions - UserSession class structure public class UserSession { public string SessionId { get; set; } = string.Empty; public string UserId { get; set; } = string.Empty; public string UserFullName { get; set; } = string.Empty; public string EntityId { get; set; } = string.Empty; // Critical for Entity-Based Request Flow public string EntityName { get; set; } = string.Empty; public string EntityTypeId { get; set; } = string.Empty; // Additional session properties... } ### Controller Integration Pattern // All controllers inherit from BaseController following Project-Specific Patterns public class MyController : BaseController { private readonly UserSessionService _userSessionService; public MyController(UserSessionService userSessionService) { _userSessionService = userSessionService; } public IActionResult MyEndpoint() { var session = GetCurrentSession(); // From BaseController var entityId = session?.EntityId; // Entity-Based Request Flow // Database queries scoped by user's EntityId var data = _context.SomeTable.Where(x => x.EntityId == entityId); return Ok(data); } } ## 3. Session Flow Implementation ### Login Process (from login.html) // 1. User authenticates with entity selection const loginData = { username: username.trim(), password: password, entityId: parseInt(entityId) // Entity context is critical }; // 2. Backend validates and creates session const response = await fetch(AppConfig.getApiUrl('auth/login'), { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(loginData) }); // 3. Frontend receives only token, full session stays on backend if (data.success && data.token) { sessionStorage.setItem('authToken', data.token); // Additional user/entity info stored for UI display only sessionStorage.setItem('entityId', data.entity.id.toString()); sessionStorage.setItem('entityName', data.entity.name); } ### API Request Flow // From index.html - All API calls include auth token fetch(AppConfig.getApiUrl('systemAttributes'), { headers: { 'Authorization': Bearer ${sessionStorage.getItem('authToken')} } }) ## 4. Entity-Based Request Scoping The session management ensures Entity-Based Request Flow: // Frontend: User's entity context preserved in session const entityId = sessionStorage.getItem('entityId'); // For UI display only // Backend: Full session with EntityId used for data access var session = GetCurrentSession(); var userEntityId = session?.EntityId; var schools = _context.Schools.Where(s => s.OwnerId == userEntityId); ## 5. Session Validation Pattern ### Frontend Authentication Check // From login.html - Minimal validation for redirects function checkAuthentication() { const authToken = sessionStorage.getItem('authToken'); const userId = sessionStorage.getItem('userId'); const entityId = sessionStorage.getItem('entityId'); if (!authToken || !userId || !entityId) { // Redirect to login window.location.href = 'login.html?error=session_expired'; return false; } return true; } ### Backend Session Retrieval (from coding instructions) // BaseController provides session access public class BaseController : ControllerBase { protected UserSession? GetCurrentSession() { // Extract token from Authorization header var authHeader = Request.Headers["Authorization"].FirstOrDefault(); if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(authHeader)) return null; var token = authHeader.Substring("Bearer ".Length).Trim(); // Retrieve full session from UserSessionService return _userSessionService.GetSessionByToken(token); } } ## 6. Key Implementation Benefits ### Security Patterns Compliance - Frontend: Minimal sensitive data exposure (token only) - Backend: Full session state managed server-side - Validation: Entity-based access control on every request ### Entity-Based Request Flow - Session Context: User's EntityId preserved throughout session - Data Scoping: All database queries filtered by user's entity - Multi-tenancy: Achieved through entity-based data isolation ### Session Lifecycle - Creation: During login with entity selection - Storage: In-memory on backend via UserSessionService - Validation: On every API request via BaseController - Cleanup: Automatic token expiry and session cleanup ## 7. Current Implementation Status From the code analysis, the frontend properly implements: ✅ Token-only storage in sessionStorage ✅ Authorization headers on API calls ✅ Entity context preservation for UI ✅ Authentication validation with redirects The backend session management (UserSessionService, BaseController) is referenced in the coding instructions but would need to be implemented in the actual API controllers to complete the Authentication & Session Management pattern. This architecture ensures that sensitive session data remains on the backend while providing secure, entity-scoped access to resources following the Entity-Based Request Flow pattern specified in the coding instructions.

content.copilot: You're absolutely right! The problem is that you're passing a string value from session storage to a query that expects an integer. Looking at the error, EF is trying to read an integer column as a string because your query parameter is being treated as a string. ## The Issue In your EntitiesController.cs, you're likely getting entityId from session storage like this: // Frontend - session storage values are always strings sessionStorage.getItem('entityId') // Returns "7" (string) But your database column owner is an integer, and EF expects the parameter to be an integer. ## The Fix Convert the string parameter to an integer before using it in your query: `csharp [HttpGet("schools")] public async Task<IActionResult> GetSchools([FromQuery] int? entityId = null) { try { // Get session and validate authentication var session = GetCurrentSession(); if (session == null) { return Unauthorized(new { success = false, message = "Authentication required" }); } // Convert entityId to integer - this is the key fix int filterEntityId; if (entityId.HasValue) { filterEntityId = entityId.Value; // Already an int from query parameter } else { // Fallback to session entity ID, ensure it's converted to int if (!int.TryParse(session.EntityId, out filterEntityId)) { _logger.LogWarning("Invalid entity ID in session: {EntityId}", session.EntityId); return BadRequest(new { success = false, message = "Invalid entity ID" }); } } _logger.LogInformation("Loading schools for entity ID: {EntityId}", filterEntityId); var schoolsQuery = _context.Entities .Include(e => e.EntityType) .AsNoTracking() .Where(e => e.IsActive && e.OwnerId == filterEntityId); // Now using int, not string var schools = await schoolsQuery .Select(e => new SchoolDto { Id = e.Id, Name = e.Name ?? string.Empty, Symbol = e.Symbol, Address = e.Address, PrincipalName = e.PrincipalName, InspectorName = e.InspectorName, Characterization = e.Characterization, ContactPerson = e.ContactPerson, EducationStage = e.EducationStage, OwnerId = e.OwnerId, EntityTypeId = e.EntityTypeId, EntityTypeName = e.EntityType != null ? e.EntityType.Name : "Unknown", IsActive = e.IsActive }) .OrderBy(e => e.Name) .ToListAsync(); _logger.LogInformation("Loaded {Count} schools for entity {EntityId}", schools.Count, filterEntityId); return Ok(schools); } catch (Exception ex) { _logger.LogError(ex, "Error loading schools"); return StatusCode(500, new { success = false, message = "שגיאה בטעינת רשימת בתי הספר", error = ex.Message }); } } ## Key Points 1. Query parameters are automatically converted: When you use [FromQuery] int? entityId, ASP.NET Core automatically converts the string query parameter to an integer. 2. Session values are strings: Values from UserSession (like session.EntityId) are stored as strings and need explicit conversion. 3. Use int.TryParse(): Always use TryParse` when converting session string values to integers to handle invalid data gracefully. This follows your coding instructions for Entity-Based Request Flow and ensures proper type handling between frontend session storage and backend database queries.

content.copilot: ## Authentication Fallback Pattern in Frontend Code This code snippet implements a graceful degradation strategy for handling unauthenticated or invalid session states in the Petel Educational Management System's frontend. The condition checks two scenarios: first, whether the authToken variable is falsy (meaning it could be null, undefined, an empty string, or not set at all), and second, whether it's explicitly the string 'undefined'. This second check is necessary because sessionStorage.getItem() returns the string 'undefined' rather than the actual undefined value when a key doesn't exist or was previously set to undefined. When either condition is true, the code takes a development-friendly approach by logging an error message to the console with an emoji marker for easy visual identification during debugging. Rather than blocking the user interface entirely or showing a blank screen, it switches to using mock data generated by the generateMockData() function. This pattern is particularly useful during local development when the backend API might not be running, or when testing UI components independently of the authentication system. The mock data is stored in the allCouncils variable (maintaining consistency with how real API data would be stored) and then passed to initializeTableWithData() to populate the ReusableTable component. Here's the fix: `csharp // ...existing code... protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder) { base.OnModelCreating(modelBuilder); // ...existing code... // Configure Document entities modelBuilder.Entity<Document>(entity => { entity.ToTable("documents", "petel_schema"); entity.Property(e => e.Description) .HasColumnName("description") .HasMaxLength(500); entity.Property(e => e.DocumentTypeId) .HasColumnName("document_type_id"); entity.Property(e => e.StatusId) .HasColumnName("status_id"); entity.Property(e => e.FileBlob) .HasColumnName("file_blob"); entity.Property(e => e.FileEncoding) .HasColumnName("file_encoding") .HasMaxLength(10) .IsRequired(); entity.Property(e => e.Version) .HasColumnName("version"); entity.Property(e => e.IsLastVersion) .HasColumnName("is_last_version"); entity.Property(e => e.CreatedAt) .HasColumnName("created_at") .HasDefaultValueSql("CURRENT_TIMESTAMP"); entity.HasOne(d => d.DocumentType) .WithMany() .HasForeignKey(d => d.DocumentTypeId) .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict); entity.HasMany(d => d.DocumentLinks) .WithOne(dl => dl.Document) .HasForeignKey(dl => dl.DocumentId) .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Cascade); }); modelBuilder.Entity<DocumentType>(entity => { entity.ToTable("document_types", "petel_schema"); // ✅ Lowercase table name with schema entity.HasKey(e => e.Id); entity.Property(e => e.Id) .HasColumnName("id"); entity.Property(e => e.Name) .HasColumnName("name") .HasMaxLength(100) .IsRequired(); entity.Property(e => e.Level) .HasColumnName("level") .HasMaxLength(50); entity.Property(e => e.YearId) .HasColumnName("year_id"); }); modelBuilder.Entity<DocumentLink>(entity => { entity.ToTable("document_links", "petel_schema"); // ✅ Lowercase table name with schema entity.HasKey(e => e.Id); entity.Property(e => e.Id) .HasColumnName("id"); entity.Property(e => e.DocumentId) .HasColumnName("document_id"); entity.Property(e => e.SchoolStudentId) .HasColumnName("school_student_id"); entity.Property(e => e.EntityId) .HasColumnName("entity_id"); entity.HasOne(dl => dl.Document) .WithMany(d => d.DocumentLinks) .HasForeignKey(dl => dl.DocumentId) .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Cascade); entity.HasIndex(e => new { e.DocumentId, e.EntityId }); entity.HasIndex(e => new { e.DocumentId, e.SchoolStudentId }); }); } // ...existing code... ## Key Changes: 1. ✅ Table names in lowercase with snake_case: "documents", "document_types", "document_links" 2. ✅ Explicit schema: "petel_schema" for all tables 3. ✅ Column names in snake_case: "id", "document_id", "file_blob", etc. 4. ✅ HasColumnName() for all properties: Maps C# PascalCase to PostgreSQL snake_case ## PostgreSQL Naming Convention Pattern: Following the project's pattern (based on existing tables like school_students, hebrew_years, etc.): - Tables: lowercase_snake_case (e.g., document_links) - Columns: lowercase_snake_case (e.g., document_type_id) - Schema: petel_schema (explicit) - Entity Framework: Use ToTable("table_name", "schema") and HasColumnName("column_name")` This matches the PostgreSQL convention used throughout your database where all identifiers are lowercase with underscores.

Hardcoded API URL in Frontend ⚠️ HIGH RISK Location: const AppConfig = { apiBaseUrl: 'http://localhost:5082/api', // ❌ HARDCODED // ... }; Also duplicated in: (line 274) Risks: - Exposed in browser console via - Cannot change environments without code modification - Breaks in production/staging deployments - Visible in browser DevTools and source code --- ### 2. Session Token Exposed in sessionStorage ⚠️ MEDIUM RISK Location: Throughout frontend code sessionStorage.setItem('authToken', token); // Visible in DevTools Risks: - Token visible in browser DevTools → Application → Storage - Vulnerable to XSS attacks that can read sessionStorage - No encryption or obfuscation --- ### 3. Detailed Error Messages Leaked to Client ⚠️ MEDIUM RISK Examples: (line 86): return StatusCode(500, new { success = false, message = "שגיאה בטעינת נתוני תלמידים", error = ex.Message // ❌ Exposes internal error details }); Risks: - Stack traces, database errors, internal paths exposed - Helps attackers understand system architecture - OWASP violation: Information Disclosure --- ### 4. CORS Wildcard in Development ⚠️ LOW RISK (Dev Only) Location: (line 32) policy.WithOrigins("http://localhost:3000", "http://127.0.0.1:3000") Risk: If accidentally deployed to production with AllowAnyOrigin(), allows all domains. --- ### 5. Database Connection String Visible ⚠️ HIGH RISK Location: "ConnectionStrings": { "DefaultConnection": "Host=localhost;Database=petel_db;Username=postgres;Password=YourPassword" } Risks: - Credentials in source control if not properly gitignored - Visible in deployed configuration files - Password hardcoded instead of using secrets manager --- ### 6. Session Data Stored in Memory Without Encryption ⚠️ LOW RISK Location: private readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, UserSession> _sessions = new(); Risks: - Session data lost on app restart - No encryption at rest - Vulnerable to memory dump attacks --- ## Recommended Fixes ### Fix 1: Environment-Based Configuration for API URL Create: (dynamic version) // ✅ SECURE: Load API URL from environment variable or build-time injection const AppConfig = { // Option A: Use environment variable (requires build tool like Vite/Webpack) apiBaseUrl: import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL || process.env.REACT_APP_API_URL || // Option B: Default to relative path (same domain deployment) '/api', getApiUrl(endpoint) { return ${this.apiBaseUrl}/${endpoint}; }, // ✅ SECURE: Don't expose config in console // Remove: window.AppConfig = AppConfig; }; // ❌ DON'T expose globally - use module imports instead // window.AppConfig = AppConfig; export default AppConfig; For vanilla JS without build tools, create a server-rendered config endpoint: Backend: Add ConfigController.cs [ApiController] [Route("api/[controller]")] [AllowAnonymous] public class ConfigController : ControllerBase { private readonly IConfiguration _configuration; public ConfigController(IConfiguration configuration) { _configuration = configuration; } [HttpGet("client")] public IActionResult GetClientConfig() { return Ok(new { apiBaseUrl = _configuration["ClientConfig:ApiBaseUrl"] ?? "/api", environment = _configuration["Environment"] ?? Application Insights (optional but recommended) - Tier: Pay-as-you-go (first 5GB/month free) - Monthly Cost: ~$0-2/month for low traffic - Why: Essential for debugging production issues --- ## Total Estimated Monthly Cost: ~$26-35 USD --- ## Deployment Configuration ### App Service Settings { "ConnectionStrings": { "DefaultConnection": "Host={your-postgres-server}.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username={admin-user};Password={password};SSL Mode=Require;" }, "Database": { "SchemaName": "petel_schema" }, "AzureStorage": { "ConnectionString": "DefaultEndpointsProtocol=https;AccountName={storage-account};AccountKey={key};EndpointSuffix=core.windows.net", "ContainerName": "documents" } } ### PostgreSQL Configuration # Enable extensions (one-time setup) CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "uuid-ossp"; content.copilot: # Azure Deployment - Test and Production Environments ## Recommended Multi-Environment Strategy ### Environment Architecture Overview ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ DEVELOPMENT (Local) │ │ - Local PostgreSQL │ │ - dotnet run (localhost:5082) │ │ - npx serve (localhost:3000) │ │ Cost: $0/month │ └─────────────────────────────────────────┘ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ TEST ENVIRONMENT (Azure) │ │ - App Service B1 │ │ - PostgreSQL Burstable B1ms │ │ - Shared with development data │ │ Cost: ~$27/month │ └─────────────────────────────────────────┘ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENT (Azure) │ │ - App Service B1 (or B2 if needed) │ │ - PostgreSQL Burstable B1ms │ │ - Production data only │ │ Cost: ~$27-40/month │ └─────────────────────────────────────────┘ Total Azure Cost: ~$54-67/month (Test + Production) --- ## Option 1: Separate Resources (Recommended) Complete isolation between Test and Production environments. ### Resource Structure Subscription ├── petel-test-rg (Resource Group) │ ├── petel-test-plan (App Service Plan B1) │ ├── petel-test-api (App Service) │ ├── petel-test-db (PostgreSQL Flexible Server B1ms) │ └── petelteststorage (Storage Account) │ └── petel-prod-rg (Resource Group) ├── petel-prod-plan (App Service Plan B1) ├── petel-prod-api (App Service) ├── petel-prod-db (PostgreSQL Flexible Server B1ms) └── petelprod storage (Storage Account) ### Deployment Commands # ============================================== # CREATE TEST ENVIRONMENT # ============================================== # 1. Create Test Resource Group az group create \ --name petel-test-rg \ --location westeurope # 2. Configure Test App Service az webapp config appsettings set \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --name petel-test-api \ --settings \ ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Test \ ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection="Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb_test;Username=peteldbadmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require" \ Database__SchemaName=petel_schema # ============================================== # CREATE PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENT # ============================================== # 1. Create Production Resource Group az group create \ --name petel-prod-rg \ --location westeurope # 2. Create Production App Service Plan az appservice plan create \ --name petel-prod-plan \ --resource-group petel-prod-rg \ --sku B1 \ --is-linux # 3. Create Production App Service az webapp create \ --name petel-prod-api \ --resource-group petel-prod-rg \ --plan petel-prod-plan \ --runtime "DOTNET:9.0" # 4. Build backend cd PetelApp.Api dotnet publish -c Release -o ./publish # 2. Copy TEST frontend config cd ../petelapp-frontend cp public/env-config.test.js public/env-config.js # 3. PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENT ├─ Merge 'develop' → 'main' ├─ Create release tag (v1.0.0) ├─ ./deploy-prod.sh ├─ Run smoke tests └─ Monitor Application Insights --- ## Security Best Practices ### Connection String Management ❌ NEVER commit passwords to Git # Store in Azure Key Vault (recommended) az keyvault create \ --name petel-keyvault \ --resource-group petel-prod-rg \ --location westeurope az keyvault secret set \ --vault-name petel-keyvault \ --name "DbConnectionString" \ --value "Host=petel-prod-db...;Password=SecurePassword" # Reference in App Service az webapp config appsettings set \ --resource-group petel-prod-rg \ --name petel-prod-api \ --settings \ ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection="@Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=https://petel-keyvault.vault.azure.net/secrets/DbConnectionString)" ### Database Firewall Rules # Allow only App Service IPs az postgres flexible-server firewall-rule create \ --resource-group petel-prod-rg \ --name petel-prod-db \ --rule-name AllowProdAppService \ --start-ip-address <app-service-outbound-ip> \ --end-ip-address <app-service-outbound-ip> # Allow Azure services (for migrations from Azure CLI) az postgres flexible-server firewall-rule create \ --resource-group petel-prod-rg \ --name petel-prod-db \ --rule-name AllowAzureServices \ --start-ip-address 0.0.0.0 \ --end-ip-address 0.0.0.0 --- ## Monitoring and Alerts ### Application Insights Queries // Failed requests in last hour requests | where timestamp > ago(1h) | where success == false | summarize count() by resultCode, operation_Name // Slow database queries dependencies | where timestamp > ago(1h) | where type == "SQL" | where duration > 1000 // > 1 second | project timestamp, name, duration, resultCode // User sessions customEvents | where name == "UserLogin" | summarize count() by bin(timestamp, 1h) ### Cost Alerts # Set budget alert az consumption budget create \ --resource-group petel-prod-rg \ --budget-name monthly-budget \ --amount 50 \ --time-grain Monthly \ --time-period startDate=2025-01-01 \ --notifications \ actual=80 \ email=admin@petel-system.co.il --- ## Summary Recommendation For Petel Application: ✅ Use Option 1: Separate Resources - Cleaner separation of concerns - Independent scaling - Easier to manage firewall rules - Can delete test resources when not needed Estimated Monthly Cost: $54 (Test + Production) Start with: - Test: B1 App Service + B1ms PostgreSQL - Production: B1 App Service + B1ms PostgreSQL Scale up when: - More than 50 concurrent users → Upgrade to B2 - Database CPU >70% → Upgrade to B2ms - Storage >100GB → Add more storage This provides a production-ready, cost-effective multi-environment setup with clear separation and easy deployment workflows.

DB_NAME="petelappdb" DB_SCHEMA="petel_schema" # Create PostgreSQL Flexible Server az postgres flexible-server create \ --name $DB_SERVER_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --location $LOCATION \ --admin-user $DB_ADMIN_USER \ --admin-password $DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD \ --sku-name Standard_B1ms \ --tier Burstable \ --storage-size 32 \ --version 16 \ --public-access 0.0.0.0 # Allow Azure services (restrict later) # ⚠️ Note: This command may take 5-10 minutes ### 2.2 Configure Firewall Rules # Allow Azure services az postgres flexible-server firewall-rule create \ --name $DB_SERVER_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --rule-name "AllowAzureServices" \ --start-ip-address 0.0.0.0 \ --end-ip-address 0.0.0.0 # Allow your local IP (for management) MY_IP=$(curl -s https://api.ipify.org) az postgres flexible-server firewall-rule create \ --name $DB_SERVER_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --rule-name "AllowMyIP" \ --start-ip-address $MY_IP \ --end-ip-address $MY_IP ### 2.3 Create Database # Create database az postgres flexible-server db create \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --server-name $DB_SERVER_NAME \ --database-name $DB_NAME ### 2.4 Get Connection String # Get server FQDN DB_SERVER_FQDN=$(az postgres flexible-server show \ --name $DB_SERVER_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --query "fullyQualifiedDomainName" \ --output tsv) echo "Database Server: $DB_SERVER_FQDN" # Connection string format: echo "Host=$DB_SERVER_FQDN;Database=$DB_NAME;Username=$DB_ADMIN_USER;Password=$DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" ### 2.5 Create Schema (using psql or Azure Portal) -- Connect using psql or Azure Data Studio -- Connection string: postgresql://PetelAdmin@petel-test-db:YourSecurePassword123!@petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com:5432/petelappdb?sslmode=require CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS petel_schema; -- Grant permissions GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA petel_schema TO "PetelAdmin"; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA petel_schema TO "PetelAdmin"; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA petel_schema TO "PetelAdmin"; --- ## Step 3: Connect App Service to Database ### 3.1 Update App Service Connection String # Build connection string CONNECTION_STRING="Host=$DB_SERVER_FQDN;Database=$DB_NAME;Username=$DB_ADMIN_USER;Password=$DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" # Set connection string in App Service az webapp config connection-string set \ --name $WEB_APP_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --connection-string-type PostgreSQL \ --settings DefaultConnection="$CONNECTION_STRING" ### 3.2 Update App Settings for Database Schema az webapp config appsettings set \ --name $WEB_APP_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --settings \ Database__SchemaName="petel_schema" --- ## Verification Checklist ### ✅ App Service - [ ] Resource group created: petel-test-rg - [ ] App Service Plan created: petel-test-plan (Linux, B1) - [ ] Web App created: petel-test-api (.NET 9.0) - [ ] HTTPS-only enabled - [ ] App URL accessible: https://petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net ### ✅ PostgreSQL Database - [ ] PostgreSQL server created: petel-test-db (v16) - [ ] Database created: petelappdb - [ ] Schema created: petel_schema - [ ] Firewall rules configured (Azure services + your IP) - [ ] Admin user: PetelAdmin - [ ] Connection string saved ### ✅ Integration - [ ] Connection string configured in App Service - [ ] Database schema setting configured - [ ] App can connect to database (test after deployment) --- ## Quick Reference App Service URL: https://petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net Database Connection (from local): Host: petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com Port: 5432 Database: petelappdb Schema: petel_schema Username: PetelAdmin Password: [Your password] SSL: Required Connection String (for appsettings.json): { "ConnectionStrings": { "DefaultConnection": "Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" }, "Database": { "SchemaName": "petel_schema" } } --- ## Next Steps (After This Setup) 1. content.copilot: # Fix: Register PostgreSQL Resource Provider This error means your Azure subscription needs to register the PostgreSQL resource provider before you can create PostgreSQL databases. ## Solution: Register the Provider ### Option 1: Using Azure CLI (Fastest) # Register the PostgreSQL resource provider az provider register --namespace Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL # Check registration status (takes 1-2 minutes) az provider show --namespace Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL --query "registrationState" # Wait until it returns "Registered" # You can also use this command to wait automatically: az provider register --namespace Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL --wait Expected output after registration: "Registered" ### Option 2: Using Azure Portal 1. Navigate to Subscriptions: - Go to [Azure Portal](https://portal.azure.com) - Search for "Subscriptions" in the top search bar - Click on your subscription 2. Register Resource Provider: - In the left menu, click "Resource providers" - Search for "Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL" - Click on the provider row - Click "Register" button at the top - Wait 1-2 minutes for status to change to "Registered" 3. Verify Registration: - Refresh the page - Status should show "Registered" --- ## After Registration: Continue with PostgreSQL Creation Once registered, re-run the PostgreSQL creation command: # Set variables (if not already set) RESOURCE_GROUP="petel-test-rg" LOCATION="westeurope" DB_SERVER_NAME="petel-test-db" DB_ADMIN_USER="PetelAdmin" DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD="YourSecurePassword123!" # ⚠️ Change this! # Create PostgreSQL Flexible Server az postgres flexible-server create \ --name $DB_SERVER_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --location $LOCATION \ --admin-user $DB_ADMIN_USER \ --admin-password $DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD \ --sku-name Standard_B1ms \ --tier Burstable \ --storage-size 32 \ --version 16 \ --public-access 0.0.0.0 # This will take 5-10 minutes --- ## Verification Checklist ✅ Check provider registration status: az provider show --namespace Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL --query "{Namespace:namespace, State:registrationState}" Expected output: { "Namespace": "Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL", "State": "Registered" } ✅ List all registered providers (optional): az provider list --query "[?registrationState=='Registered'].namespace" --output table --- ## Common Registration Issues ### Issue: "You do not have permission to register providers" Cause: Your Azure account lacks subscription-level permissions. Solution: Ask subscription owner/admin to: 1. Grant you "Contributor" or "Owner" role at subscription level, OR 2. Register the provider for you Alternative: Use Azure Portal instead of CLI (sometimes has different permission requirements) --- ### Issue: Registration stuck in "Registering" state Cause: Azure backend processing delay. Solution: # Wait up to 5 minutes az provider register --namespace Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL --wait # If still stuck after 5 minutes, unregister and re-register az provider unregister --namespace Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL az provider register --namespace Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL --wait --- ## Other Providers You May Need For complete Petel deployment, you may also need: # App Service (Web Apps) az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Web # Storage Accounts (for documents) az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Storage # Application Insights (monitoring) az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Insights # Register all at once and wait az provider register --namespace Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL --wait az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Web --wait az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Storage --wait az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Insights --wait Check all registrations: az provider show --namespace Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL --query "registrationState" az provider show --namespace Microsoft.Web --query "registrationState" az provider show --namespace Microsoft.Storage --query "registrationState" az provider show --namespace Microsoft.Insights --query "registrationState" All should return: "Registered" --- ## Next Steps Once PostgreSQL provider is registered: 1. ✅ Re-run Step 2.1 (Create PostgreSQL Flexible Server) 2. ✅ Continue with Step 2.2 (Configure Firewall Rules) 3. ✅ Continue with Step 2.3 (Create Database) 4. ✅ Continue with Step 2.4 (Get Connection String) 5. ✅ Continue with Step 2.5 (Create Schema) --- ## Quick Resume Script After registration completes, run this to continue: # Resume from Step 2.1 RESOURCE_GROUP="petel-test-rg" LOCATION="westeurope" DB_SERVER_NAME="petel-test-db" DB_ADMIN_USER="PetelAdmin" DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD="YourSecurePassword123!" DB_NAME="petelappdb" # Create PostgreSQL server az postgres flexible-server create \ --name $DB_SERVER_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --location $LOCATION \ --admin-user $DB_ADMIN_USER \ --admin-password $DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD \ --sku-name Standard_B1ms \ --tier Burstable \ --storage-size 32 \ --version 16 \ --public-access 0.0.0.0 # Allow Azure services az postgres flexible-server firewall-rule create \ --name $DB_SERVER_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --rule-name "AllowAzureServices" \ --start-ip-address 0.0.0.0 \ --end-ip-address 0.0.0.0 # Allow your local IP MY_IP=$(curl -s https://api.ipify.org) az postgres flexible-server firewall-rule create \ --name $DB_SERVER_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --rule-name "AllowMyIP" \ --start-ip-address $MY_IP \ --end-ip-address $MY_IP # Create database az postgres flexible-server db create \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --server-name $DB_SERVER_NAME \ --database-name $DB_NAME echo "✅ PostgreSQL setup complete!" echo "Server: $DB_SERVER_NAME.postgres.database.azure.com" echo "Database: $DB_NAME" --- Let me know once the provider is registered and I'll help you continue with the deployment! 🚀

content.copilot: # Fix PostgreSQL Database for Hebrew/Israel Configuration Your PostgreSQL database needs to be reconfigured for proper Hebrew text support with Israeli locale settings. ## Problem The database was created with: - ❌ Charset: UTF8 (correct) - ❌ Collation: en_US.utf8 (wrong - English US) - ❌ CType: en_US.utf8 (wrong - English US) ## Solution: Recreate Database with Hebrew Locale ### Step 1: Drop and Recreate Database ⚠️ WARNING: This will delete all data. Only do this on TEST environment. # Set variables RESOURCE_GROUP="petel-test-rg" DB_SERVER_NAME="petel-test-db" DB_ADMIN_USER="PetelAdmin" DB_NAME="petelappdb" # Connect to PostgreSQL server psql "host=$DB_SERVER_NAME.postgres.database.azure.com port=5432 dbname=postgres user=$DB_ADMIN_USER sslmode=require" Inside psql: -- 1. Terminate active connections SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pg_stat_activity.pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE pg_stat_activity.datname = 'petelappdb' AND pid <> pg_backend_pid(); -- 2. Drop existing database DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS petelappdb; -- 3. Create database with Hebrew locale CREATE DATABASE petelappdb WITH OWNER = "PetelAdmin" ENCODING = 'UTF8' LC_COLLATE = 'he_IL.UTF-8' LC_CTYPE = 'he_IL.UTF-8' TEMPLATE = template0; -- 4. Verify locale settings \c petelappdb SHOW LC_COLLATE; SHOW LC_CTYPE; SHOW SERVER_ENCODING; -- Expected output: -- LC_COLLATE | he_IL.UTF-8 -- LC_CTYPE | he_IL.UTF-8 -- SERVER_ENCODING | UTF8 ### Step 2: Create Schema and Extensions -- Still connected to petelappdb -- Create schema CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS petel_schema; -- Grant permissions GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA petel_schema TO "PetelAdmin"; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA petel_schema TO "PetelAdmin"; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA petel_schema TO "PetelAdmin"; -- Enable extensions CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "uuid-ossp"; -- Set default schema search path ALTER DATABASE petelappdb SET search_path TO petel_schema, public; -- Verify schema \dn petel_schema ### Step 3: Run EF Core Migrations # From your local machine cd PetelApp.Api # Set connection string with Hebrew database $env:ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection="Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" # Run migrations to create tables dotnet ef database update --context AppDbContext # Verify tables created dotnet ef migrations list --context AppDbContext --- ## Alternative: If Locale Not Available If he_IL.UTF-8 locale is not available on Azure PostgreSQL: ### Option A: Use en_US.UTF-8 with Explicit Collation -- Database with UTF8 encoding (supports Hebrew characters) CREATE DATABASE petelappdb WITH OWNER = "PetelAdmin" ENCODING = 'UTF8' LC_COLLATE = 'en_US.utf8' LC_CTYPE = 'en_US.utf8' TEMPLATE = template0; -- Then use explicit collation in queries SELECT FROM students ORDER BY student_name COLLATE "he_IL" ASC; ### Option B: Use C Locale (Binary Sorting) -- C locale = byte-by-byte comparison (works with any UTF8 text) CREATE DATABASE petelappdb WITH OWNER = "PetelAdmin" ENCODING = 'UTF8' LC_COLLATE = 'C' LC_CTYPE = 'C' TEMPLATE = template0; Pros: Always available, predictable sorting Cons: Sorting may not follow Hebrew alphabetical order --- ## Check Available Locales on Azure PostgreSQL -- Connect to postgres database \c postgres -- List all available locales SELECT FROM pg_collation WHERE collname LIKE '%he%' OR collname LIKE '%IL%'; -- List all installed locales SHOW LC_COLLATE; Common available locales on Azure: - en_US.utf8 (default) - C (binary) - he_IL.utf8 (may need to be installed) --- ## Azure CLI: Recreate Database # Delete existing database az postgres flexible-server db delete \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --server-name $DB_SERVER_NAME \ --database-name $DB_NAME \ --yes # Create new database (locale set during creation if supported) az postgres flexible-server db create \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --server-name $DB_SERVER_NAME \ --database-name $DB_NAME Note: Azure CLI does not expose locale parameters. You must set locale via SQL after creation. --- ## Verification Script After recreating database: -- Connect to your database \c petelappdb -- Verify settings SELECT datname AS database_name, pg_encoding_to_char(encoding) AS encoding, datcollate AS collation, datctype AS ctype FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'petelappdb'; -- Test Hebrew text storage CREATE TEMP TABLE test_hebrew ( id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, hebrew_text TEXT ); INSERT INTO test_hebrew (hebrew_text) VALUES ('שלום עולם'), ('תלמיד'), ('בית ספר'), ('אבגדהוזחטיכלמנסעפצקרשת'); SELECT * FROM test_hebrew ORDER BY hebrew_text; -- Verify sorting works correctly -- Expected: alphabetical Hebrew order (א before ת) DROP TABLE test_hebrew; --- ## Update Backend Configuration appsettings.Test.json: { "ConnectionStrings": { "DefaultConnection": "Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true;CommandTimeout=120" }, "Database": { "SchemaName": "petel_schema" }, "Logging": { "LogLevel": { "Default": "Information", "Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore": "Information" } } } Update App Service connection string: CONNECTION_STRING="Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" az webapp config connection-string set \ --name petel-test-api \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --connection-string-type PostgreSQL \ --settings DefaultConnection="$CONNECTION_STRING" --- ## Hebrew Text Best Practices After fixing database locale: ### Backend (EF Core) // Entity configuration for Hebrew text fields public class StudentConfiguration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<Student> { public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<Student> builder) { builder.ToTable("students"); // Hebrew text columns builder.Property(e => e.FirstName) .HasMaxLength(100) .IsRequired() .HasColumnType("varchar(100)"); // UTF8 varchar builder.Property(e => e.LastName) .HasMaxLength(100) .IsRequired() .HasColumnType("varchar(100)"); // Indexes for Hebrew text (case-sensitive by default with he_IL locale) builder.HasIndex(e => e.LastName) .HasDatabaseName("idx_students_last_name"); } } ### Queries with Hebrew Collation // Explicit collation in LINQ (if needed) var students = await _context.Students .OrderBy(s => EF.Functions.Collate(s.LastName, "he_IL")) .ToListAsync(); // Case-insensitive search for Hebrew var results = await _context.Students .Where(s => EF.Functions.ILike(s.FirstName, $"%{searchTerm}%")) .ToListAsync(); ### Frontend Hebrew Text Handling // Proper Hebrew string comparison function compareHebrewStrings(a, b) { return a.localeCompare(b, 'he-IL', { sensitivity: 'base' }); } // Sort Hebrew array const hebrewNames = ['תלמיד', 'בית ספר', 'אבג']; hebrewNames.sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b, 'he-IL')); --- ## Complete Recreate Script Bash script for complete database recreation: #!/bin/bash # recreate-hebrew-db.sh RESOURCE_GROUP="petel-test-rg" DB_SERVER_NAME="petel-test-db" DB_ADMIN_USER="PetelAdmin" DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD="YourSecurePassword123!" DB_NAME="petelappdb" DB_SCHEMA="petel_schema" echo "🔄 Recreating database with Hebrew locale..." # Connect and recreate PGPASSWORD=$DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD psql \ "host=$DB_SERVER_NAME.postgres.database.azure.com port=5432 dbname=postgres user=$DB_ADMIN_USER sslmode=require" \ <<EOF -- Terminate connections SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pg_stat_activity.pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE pg_stat_activity.datname = '$DB_NAME' AND pid <> pg_backend_pid(); -- Drop and recreate DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS $DB_NAME; CREATE DATABASE $DB_NAME WITH OWNER = "$DB_ADMIN_USER" ENCODING = 'UTF8' LC_COLLATE = 'he_IL.UTF-8' LC_CTYPE = 'he_IL.UTF-8' TEMPLATE = template0; -- Connect to new database \c $DB_NAME -- Create schema CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS $DB_SCHEMA; GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA $DB_SCHEMA TO "$DB_ADMIN_USER"; -- Enable extensions CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "uuid-ossp"; -- Set search path ALTER DATABASE $DB_NAME SET search_path TO $DB_SCHEMA, public; -- Verify SHOW LC_COLLATE; SHOW LC_CTYPE; EOF echo "✅ Database recreated with Hebrew locale" echo "🚀 Now run: cd PetelApp.Api && dotnet ef database update" --- ## Summary For TEST environment: 1. ✅ Recreate database with he_IL.UTF-8 locale 2. ✅ Create schema petel_schema with proper permissions 3. ✅ Run EF migrations to create tables 4. ✅ Update connection strings in App Service 5. ✅ Test Hebrew text storage and sorting Verification checklist: - [ ] Database encoding = UTF8 - [ ] Database collation = he_IL.UTF-8 (or C if unavailable) - [ ] Schema petel_schema exists - [ ] Extensions enabled (uuid-ossp) - [ ] EF migrations applied successfully - [ ] Hebrew text stores correctly - [ ] Hebrew text sorts alphabetically - [ ] Connection string updated in Azure Next: After database is recreated and configured, we can proceed with deployment of the application code.

content.copilot: # Create Hangfire Database for Background Jobs Hangfire requires its own database schema to store job queues, schedules, and execution history. ## Option 1: Separate Database (Recommended for Production) ### Create Dedicated Hangfire Database # Set variables RESOURCE_GROUP="petel-test-rg" DB_SERVER_NAME="petel-test-db" DB_ADMIN_USER="PetelAdmin" HANGFIRE_DB_NAME="hangfiredb" # Create Hangfire database az postgres flexible-server db create \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --server-name $DB_SERVER_NAME \ --database-name $HANGFIRE_DB_NAME echo "✅ Hangfire database created: $HANGFIRE_DB_NAME" ### Update Connection Strings # Get server FQDN DB_SERVER_FQDN=$(az postgres flexible-server show \ --name $DB_SERVER_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --query "fullyQualifiedDomainName" \ --output tsv) # Build Hangfire connection string HANGFIRE_CONNECTION="Host=$DB_SERVER_FQDN;Database=$HANGFIRE_DB_NAME;Username=$DB_ADMIN_USER;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" echo "Hangfire Connection String:" echo "$HANGFIRE_CONNECTION" ### Update appsettings.Test.json { "ConnectionStrings": { "DefaultConnection": "Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true", "HangfireConnection": "Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=hangfiredb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" }, "Database": { "SchemaName": "petel_schema" }, "Hangfire": { "StorageSchema": "hangfire", "DashboardEnabled": true, "DashboardPath": "/hangfire" } } --- ## Option 2: Same Database, Separate Schema (Cost-Effective for TEST) ### Create Hangfire Schema in Existing Database -- Connect to petelappdb psql "host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com port=5432 dbname=petelappdb user=PetelAdmin sslmode=require" -- Create Hangfire schema CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS hangfire; -- Grant permissions GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA hangfire TO "PetelAdmin"; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA hangfire TO "PetelAdmin"; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA hangfire TO "PetelAdmin"; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA hangfire GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO "PetelAdmin"; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA hangfire GRANT ALL ON SEQUENCES TO "PetelAdmin"; -- Verify \dn hangfire ### Update appsettings.Test.json (Same Database) { "ConnectionStrings": { "DefaultConnection": "Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true", "HangfireConnection": "Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" }, "Database": { "SchemaName": "petel_schema" }, "Hangfire": { "StorageSchema": "hangfire", "DashboardEnabled": true, "DashboardPath": "/hangfire" } } --- ## Verify Hangfire Configuration in Backend ### Check Program.cs using Hangfire; using Hangfire.PostgreSql; var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); // ... existing service configuration ... // ✅ Configure Hangfire with PostgreSQL storage builder.Services.AddHangfire(configuration => configuration .SetDataCompatibilityLevel(CompatibilityLevel.Version_180) .UseSimpleAssemblyNameTypeSerializer() .UseRecommendedSerializerSettings() .UsePostgreSqlStorage(options => { options.UseNpgsqlConnection(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("HangfireConnection")); // ✅ Use separate schema var hangfireSchema = builder.Configuration.GetSection("Hangfire:StorageSchema").Value ?? "hangfire"; options.SchemaName = hangfireSchema; }) ); // ✅ Add Hangfire server builder.Services.AddHangfireServer(options => { options.WorkerCount = 1; // TEST: 1 worker, PROD: increase for scale options.ServerName = $"{Environment.MachineName}-{Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("WEBSITE_INSTANCE_ID") ?? "local"}"; }); var app = builder.Build(); // ... existing middleware ... // ✅ Enable Hangfire Dashboard (TEST/DEV only) if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment() || app.Environment.EnvironmentName == "Test") { var dashboardPath = builder.Configuration.GetSection("Hangfire:DashboardPath").Value ?? "/hangfire"; app.UseHangfireDashboard(dashboardPath, new DashboardOptions { Authorization = new[] { new HangfireAuthorizationFilter() } }); } app.Run(); ### Verify Hangfire Authorization Filter using Hangfire.Dashboard; namespace PetelApp.Api.Filters { public class HangfireAuthorizationFilter : IDashboardAuthorizationFilter { public bool Authorize(DashboardContext context) { // ⚠️ TEST: Allow all access // ⚠️ PRODUCTION: Implement proper authorization var httpContext = context.GetHttpContext(); // For TEST/DEV: Allow all if (httpContext.Request.Host.Host.Contains("localhost") || httpContext.Request.Host.Host.Contains("test")) { return true; } // For PRODUCTION: Check authentication // return httpContext.User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated ?? false; return false; } } } --- ## Initialize Hangfire Tables ### Automatic Initialization (Recommended) Hangfire will automatically create its tables on first run: # Run backend locally to initialize cd PetelApp.Api dotnet run # Or deploy to Azure and start the app # Hangfire will create tables on startup Expected Hangfire Tables (in hangfire schema): - job - Job definitions - jobqueue - Job queue - jobparameter - Job parameters - state - Job states - server - Server instances - set - Sets (recurring jobs, etc.) - counter - Counters - hash - Hash storage - list - List storage - aggregatedcounter - Aggregated counters - lock - Distributed locks - schema - Schema version ### Manual Verification (Optional) -- Connect to database psql "host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com port=5432 dbname=petelappdb user=PetelAdmin sslmode=require" -- OR for separate database: -- psql "host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com port=5432 dbname=hangfiredb user=PetelAdmin sslmode=require" -- List Hangfire schema \dn hangfire -- List Hangfire tables (after first run) \dt hangfire. -- Expected output (after initialization): -- Schema | Name | Type | Owner -- ------------------+---------------------+-------+------------- -- hangfire | aggregatedcounter | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | counter | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | hash | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | job | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | jobparameter | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | jobqueue | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | list | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | lock | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | schema | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | server | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | set | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | state | table | PetelAdmin --- ## Update Azure App Service Configuration # Set Hangfire connection string in App Service WEB_APP_NAME="petel-test-api" RESOURCE_GROUP="petel-test-rg" # Option 1: Separate database HANGFIRE_CONNECTION="Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=hangfiredb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" # Option 2: Same database, separate schema HANGFIRE_CONNECTION="Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" # Set connection string az webapp config connection-string set \ --name $WEB_APP_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --connection-string-type PostgreSQL \ --settings HangfireConnection="$HANGFIRE_CONNECTION" # Set Hangfire app settings az webapp config appsettings set \ --name $WEB_APP_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --settings \ Hangfire__StorageSchema="hangfire" \ Hangfire__DashboardEnabled="true" \ Hangfire__DashboardPath="/hangfire" echo "✅ App Service Hangfire configuration complete" --- ## Test Hangfire Setup ### 1. Access Hangfire Dashboard Local: http://localhost:5082/hangfire Azure Test: https://petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net/hangfire Expected Dashboard Sections: - Jobs (Enqueued, Scheduled, Processing, Succeeded, Failed) - Recurring Jobs - Servers (active Hangfire server instances) - Retries ### 2. Verify System Attribute Loading Job using Hangfire; using Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting; public class SystemAttributeLoaderHostedService : IHostedService { private readonly IRecurringJobManager _recurringJobManager; public SystemAttributeLoaderHostedService(IRecurringJobManager recurringJobManager) { _recurringJobManager = recurringJobManager; } public Task StartAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken) { // ✅ Schedule recurring job to load system attributes _recurringJobManager.AddOrUpdate( "load-system-attributes", () => LoadSystemAttributes(), Cron.Hourly); // Or your desired schedule return Task.CompletedTask; } public Task StopAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken) { return Task.CompletedTask; } public static void LoadSystemAttributes() { // Your system attributes loading logic Console.WriteLine("🔄 Loading system attributes..."); // ... load from database into cache Console.WriteLine("✅ System attributes loaded"); } } ### 3. Verify Job Execution -- Check Hangfire jobs SELECT j.id, j.invocationdata::json->>'Type' as job_type, s.name as state, j.createdat, s.createdat as state_time FROM hangfire.job j LEFT JOIN hangfire.state s ON s.jobid = j.id WHERE s.id = ( SELECT MAX(id) FROM hangfire.state WHERE jobid = j.id ) ORDER BY j.createdat DESC LIMIT 10; -- Check recurring jobs SELECT FROM hangfire.set WHERE key LIKE 'recurring-jobs%'; -- Check active servers SELECT * FROM hangfire.server WHERE lastheartbeat > NOW() - INTERVAL '5 minutes'; --- ## Troubleshooting ### Issue: "Schema 'hangfire' does not exist" Solution: CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS hangfire; GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA hangfire TO "PetelAdmin"; ### Issue: "Permission denied for schema hangfire" Solution: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA hangfire TO "PetelAdmin"; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA hangfire TO "PetelAdmin"; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA hangfire GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO "PetelAdmin"; ### Issue: Hangfire dashboard shows "No servers" Cause: Hangfire server not running Solution: 1. Verify AddHangfireServer() is called in Program.cs 2. Check App Service logs for Hangfire startup 3. Verify connection string is correct 4. Check Azure App Service is running ### Issue: Jobs not executing Cause: Worker count = 0 or server stopped Solution: // Program.cs builder.Services.AddHangfireServer(options => { options.WorkerCount = 1; // Must be > 0 options.ServerName = $"petel-test-{Environment.MachineName}"; }); --- ## Cost Impact ### Option 1: Separate Database - Additional Cost: ~₪44-55/month (~$12-15/month) - Pros: Complete isolation, easier backup/restore - Cons: Higher cost ### Option 2: Same Database, Separate Schema - Additional Cost: ~₪0 (only storage) - Storage Impact: ~100-500 MB (depends on job history) - Pros: Cost-effective for TEST - Cons: Shared resources, schema management Recommendation for TEST: Use Option 2 (same database, separate schema) --- ## Summary ### Quick Setup (Option 2 - Same Database) # 1. Create schema psql "host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com dbname=petelappdb user=PetelAdmin" \ -c "CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS hangfire; GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA hangfire TO PetelAdmin;" # 2. Update App Service settings az webapp config appsettings set \ --name petel-test-api \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --settings Hangfire__StorageSchema="hangfire" Hangfire__DashboardEnabled="true" # 3. Restart app (Hangfire will create tables) az webapp restart --name petel-test-api --resource-group petel-test-rg # 4. Verify dashboard # https://petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net/hangfire ### Verification Checklist - ✅ Hangfire schema created (hangfire) - ✅ Connection string configured (HangfireConnection) - ✅ App settings configured (Hangfire__StorageSchema, etc.) - ✅ Hangfire tables created automatically on first run - ✅ Dashboard accessible at /hangfire - ✅ Background jobs visible in dashboard - ✅ At least 1 active server in dashboard - ✅ System attribute loading job scheduled Next Step: Deploy the backend application to Azure and verify Hangfire dashboard is accessible.

-- Grant permissions to admin user GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA hangfire TO "PetelAdmin"; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA hangfire TO "PetelAdmin"; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA hangfire TO "PetelAdmin"; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA hangfire GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO "PetelAdmin"; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA hangfire GRANT ALL ON SEQUENCES TO "PetelAdmin"; -- Verify schemas \dn -- Expected output: -- Name | Owner -- ---------+------------ -- hangfire| PetelAdmin -- petel_schema | PetelAdmin -- public | postgres -- Exit psql \q Alternative: Using Azure CLI psql connection: # If psql command doesn't work, install Azure PostgreSQL extension az extension add --name db-up # Or connect via Azure Cloud Shell (has psql pre-installed) --- ## Step 2: Update Backend Configuration ### appsettings.Test.json { "ConnectionStrings": { "DefaultConnection": "Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true", "HangfireConnection": "Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" }, "Database": { "SchemaName": "petel_schema" }, "Hangfire": { "StorageSchema": "hangfire", "DashboardEnabled": true, "DashboardPath": "/hangfire", "WorkerCount": 1 }, "Logging": { "LogLevel": { "Default": "Information", "Microsoft.AspNetCore": "Warning", "Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore": "Information", "Hangfire": "Information" } }, "AllowedHosts": "" } --- ## Step 3: Verify Hangfire Configuration in Program.cs using Hangfire; using Hangfire.PostgreSql; using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore; using Microsoft.Extensions.Options; using PetelApp.Api.Configuration; var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); // ...existing service configuration... // ✅ Register Hangfire configuration builder.Services.Configure<HangfireSettings>( builder.Configuration.GetSection("Hangfire")); // ✅ Configure Hangfire with PostgreSQL storage (same database, different schema) builder.Services.AddHangfire((serviceProvider, configuration) => { var hangfireSettings = serviceProvider.GetRequiredService<IOptions<HangfireSettings>>().Value; var connectionString = builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("HangfireConnection"); configuration .SetDataCompatibilityLevel(CompatibilityLevel.Version_180) .UseSimpleAssemblyNameTypeSerializer() .UseRecommendedSerializerSettings() .UsePostgreSqlStorage(options => { options.UseNpgsqlConnection(connectionString); // ✅ Use separate schema (not separate database) options.SchemaName = hangfireSettings.StorageSchema; }); }); // ✅ Add Hangfire server builder.Services.AddHangfireServer(options => { var hangfireSettings = builder.Configuration.GetSection("Hangfire").Get<HangfireSettings>(); options.WorkerCount = hangfireSettings?.WorkerCount ?? 1; options.ServerName = $"petel-test-{Environment.MachineName}-{Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("WEBSITE_INSTANCE_ID") ?? "local"}"; }); var app = builder.Build(); // ...existing middleware... // ✅ Enable Hangfire Dashboard (TEST/Staging only) if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment() || app.Environment.EnvironmentName == "Test" || app.Environment.EnvironmentName == "Staging") { var hangfireSettings = app.Services.GetRequiredService<IOptions<HangfireSettings>>().Value; var dashboardPath = hangfireSettings.DashboardPath ?? "/hangfire"; app.UseHangfireDashboard(dashboardPath, new DashboardOptions { Authorization = new[] { new HangfireAuthorizationFilter() } }); } app.Run(); --- ## Step 4: Create Hangfire Configuration Class namespace PetelApp.Api.Configuration { /// <summary> /// Hangfire background job configuration settings /// </summary> public class HangfireSettings { /// <summary> /// PostgreSQL schema name for Hangfire tables (default: "hangfire") /// </summary> public string StorageSchema { get; set; } = "hangfire"; /// <summary> /// Enable Hangfire Dashboard UI (default: true for non-production) /// </summary> public bool DashboardEnabled { get; set; } = true; /// <summary> /// Hangfire Dashboard URL path (default: "/hangfire") /// </summary> public string DashboardPath { get; set; } = "/hangfire"; /// <summary> /// Number of background job worker threads (default: 1 for TEST, 5 for Production) /// </summary> public int WorkerCount { get; set; } = 1; } } --- ## Step 5: Update Azure App Service Configuration # Set variables WEB_APP_NAME="petel-test-api" RESOURCE_GROUP="petel-test-rg" DB_SERVER_FQDN="petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com" DB_NAME="petelappdb" DB_ADMIN_USER="PetelAdmin" DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD="YourSecurePassword123!" # ✅ Set Hangfire connection string (SAME database as DefaultConnection) HANGFIRE_CONNECTION="Host=$DB_SERVER_FQDN;Database=$DB_NAME;Username=$DB_ADMIN_USER;Password=$DB_ADMIN_PASSWORD;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" az webapp config connection-string set \ --name $WEB_APP_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --connection-string-type PostgreSQL \ --settings HangfireConnection="$HANGFIRE_CONNECTION" # ✅ Set Hangfire app settings az webapp config appsettings set \ --name $WEB_APP_NAME \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --settings \ Hangfire__StorageSchema="hangfire" \ Hangfire__DashboardEnabled="true" \ Hangfire__DashboardPath="/hangfire" \ Hangfire__WorkerCount="1" echo "✅ Hangfire configuration complete (using schema in existing database)" --- ## Step 6: Verify Schema Structure -- Connect to database psql "host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com dbname=petelappdb user=PetelAdmin sslmode=require" -- List all schemas \dn -- Expected: -- Name | Owner -- --------------+------------ -- hangfire | PetelAdmin ← Hangfire background jobs -- petel_schema | PetelAdmin ← Application data -- public | postgres -- Check schema permissions SELECT nspname AS schema_name, nspowner::regrole AS owner, has_schema_privilege('PetelAdmin', nspname, 'CREATE') AS can_create, has_schema_privilege('PetelAdmin', nspname, 'USAGE') AS can_use FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname IN ('petel_schema', 'hangfire'); -- Expected output: -- schema_name | owner | can_create | can_use -- --------------+------------+------------+--------- -- petel_schema | PetelAdmin | t | t -- hangfire | PetelAdmin | t | t -- Check if Hangfire tables exist (after first app run) \dt hangfire. -- Expected (after initialization): -- Schema | Name | Type | Owner -- ----------------+---------------------+-------+------------- -- hangfire | aggregatedcounter | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | counter | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | hash | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | job | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | jobparameter | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | jobqueue | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | list | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | lock | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | schema | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | server | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | set | table | PetelAdmin -- hangfire | state | table | PetelAdmin --- ## Step 7: Test Hangfire Initialization ### Run Backend Locally First cd PetelApp.Api # Set connection string temporarily for local test $env:ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection="Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" $env:ConnectionStrings__HangfireConnection="Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" # Run application dotnet run # Expected console output: # info: Hangfire.PostgreSql.PostgreSqlStorage[0] # Start installing Hangfire SQL objects... # info: Hangfire.PostgreSql.PostgreSqlStorage[0] # Hangfire SQL objects installed. # info: Microsoft.Hosting.Lifetime[14] # Now listening on: http://localhost:5082 Verify Hangfire Dashboard (local): - Open browser: http://localhost:5082/hangfire - Should show Hangfire Dashboard UI - Check "Servers" tab - should show 1 active server --- ## Complete Architecture Diagram ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Azure PostgreSQL Flexible Server (Israel Central) │ │ petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com │ │ │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Database: petelappdb (UTF8, he_IL.UTF-8) │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ │ │ Schema: petel_schema │ │ │ │ │ │ ✅ Application tables: │ │ │ │ │ │ - users │ │ │ │ │ │ - entities │ │ │ │ │ │ - schools │ │ │ │ │ │ - students │ │ │ │ │ │ - school_years │ │ │ │ │ │ - documents │ │ │ │ │ │ ... (all application tables) │ │ │ │ │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ │ │ Schema: hangfire │ │ │ │ │ │ ✅ Background job tables: │ │ │ │ │ │ - job │ │ │ │ │ │ - jobqueue │ │ │ │ │ │ - jobparameter │ │ │ │ │ │ - state │ │ │ │ │ │ - server │ │ │ │ │ │ - set │ │ │ │ │ │ ... (Hangfire infrastructure) │ │ │ │ │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ↑ ↑ │ DefaultConnection │ HangfireConnection │ (petel_schema) │ (hangfire schema) │ │ ┌────────┴──────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────┐ │ Azure App Service (Israel Central) │ │ petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net │ │ │ │ ✅ ASP.NET Core 9.0 Application │ │ ✅ Entity Framework Core → petel_schema │ │ ✅ Hangfire Background Jobs → hangfire schema │ │ ✅ Same database, isolated schemas │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ --- ## Cost Comparison ### ❌ Separate Database Approach (Avoided) PostgreSQL (petelappdb): ₪44/month PostgreSQL (hangfiredb): ₪44/month ────────────────────────────────────── Total: ₪88/month ### ✅ Schema-Based Approach (Implemented) PostgreSQL (petelappdb): ₪44/month ├─ petel_schema (application data) └─ hangfire (background jobs) ────────────────────────────────────── Total: ₪44/month 💰 Monthly Savings: ₪44 (~$12 USD) 💰 Annual Savings: ₪528 (~$144 USD) --- ## Deployment Checklist ### ✅ Completed Steps 1. ✅ Database Schema Created - hangfire schema in petelappdb database - Permissions granted to PetelAdmin - Schema verified with \dn command 2. ✅ Backend Configuration - appsettings.Test.json updated with Hangfire settings - HangfireSettings configuration class created - Program.cs configured to use schema-based storage - Same connection string for both schemas 3. ✅ Azure App Service Settings - HangfireConnection connection string set (same as DefaultConnection) - Hangfire__StorageSchema = "hangfire" - Hangfire__DashboardEnabled = "true" - Hangfire__WorkerCount = "1" --- ## Next Steps: Deploy Backend Now that infrastructure is ready, you can deploy the backend: # 1. Build backend cd PetelApp.Api dotnet publish -c Release -o ./publish # 2. Create deployment ZIP cd publish zip -r ../deploy-test.zip . cd .. # 3. Deploy to Azure az webapp deployment source config-zip \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --name petel-test-api \ --src deploy-test.zip # 4. Monitor deployment az webapp log tail --name petel-test-api --resource-group petel-test-rg # 5. Verify Hangfire initialization # Check logs for: "Hangfire SQL objects installed" # 6. Access Hangfire Dashboard # https://petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net/hangfire --- ## Verification After Deployment # 1. Check Hangfire tables were created psql "host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com dbname=petelappdb user=PetelAdmin sslmode=require" \ -c "\dt hangfire." # 2. Verify Hangfire server is running psql "host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com dbname=petelappdb user=PetelAdmin sslmode=require" \ -c "SELECT FROM hangfire.server WHERE lastheartbeat > NOW() - INTERVAL '5 minutes';" # 3. Check API health curl https://petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net/api/health # 4. Access Hangfire Dashboard # Open browser: https://petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net/hangfire # Should show dashboard with 1 active server --- ## Summary What We Did: - ✅ Created hangfire schema in existing petelappdb database - ✅ Configured Hangfire to use schema-based storage (not separate database) - ✅ Same PostgreSQL connection string for both application and Hangfire - ✅ Isolated schemas prevent table name conflicts - ✅ Saved ₪44/month (~$12 USD) by avoiding second database Database Structure: - petelappdb database with UTF8 encoding and Hebrew locale - petel_schema - Application data (students, schools, etc.) - hangfire - Background job infrastructure - public - PostgreSQL system schema Ready for Deployment: - Infrastructure configured in Azure (App Service + PostgreSQL) - Backend configured to use schema-based storage - Connection strings set in App Service - Hangfire will auto-create tables on first run Next: Deploy backend code to Azure App Service and verify Hangfire dashboard is accessible.
