content.copilot: # First-Time Azure Deployment Guide - Petel Educational Management System ## Pre-Deployment Checklist Before deploying, verify your environment is ready: ### ✅ Azure Infrastructure (Already Created) - [x] Resource Group: petel-test-rg - [x] App Service Plan: petel-test-plan (Linux B1) - [x] App Service: petel-test-api (.NET 9.0) - [x] PostgreSQL Server: petel-test-db (Flexible Server, Burstable B1ms) - [x] Database: petelappdb (UTF8, Hebrew locale) - [x] Schemas: petel_schema (application), hangfire (background jobs) - [x] Connection strings configured in App Service ### ✅ Local Development Environment # Verify .NET SDK dotnet --version # Should be 9.0.x # Verify Azure CLI az --version # Verify you're logged in to Azure az account show # Verify correct subscription az account list --output table --- ## Step 1: Prepare Backend for Deployment ### 1.1 Update Configuration Files Create/Update appsettings.Test.json: { "Logging": { "LogLevel": { "Default": "Information", "Microsoft.AspNetCore": "Warning", "Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore": "Information", "Hangfire": "Information" } }, "AllowedHosts": "", "ConnectionStrings": { "DefaultConnection": "Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=PLACEHOLDER;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true", "HangfireConnection": "Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=PLACEHOLDER;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" }, "Database": { "SchemaName": "petel_schema" }, "Hangfire": { "StorageSchema": "hangfire", "DashboardEnabled": true, "DashboardPath": "/hangfire", "WorkerCount": 1 }, "Cors": { "AllowedOrigins": [ "https://petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net" ] } } Note: Connection string passwords will be set via Azure App Service configuration (not in source control). ### 1.2 Update Program.cs for Azure Environment Verify CORS and environment configuration: // ...existing code... // ✅ CORS configuration var corsOrigins = builder.Configuration.GetSection("Cors:AllowedOrigins").Get<string[]>() ?? new[] { "http://localhost:3000" }; builder.Services.AddCors(options => { options.AddPolicy("AllowFrontend", policy => { policy.WithOrigins(corsOrigins) .AllowAnyHeader() .AllowAnyMethod() .AllowCredentials(); }); }); var app = builder.Build(); // ✅ Use CORS app.UseCors("AllowFrontend"); // ✅ Enable Hangfire Dashboard (TEST environment only) if (app.Environment.EnvironmentName == "Test" || app.Environment.EnvironmentName == "Staging" || app.Environment.IsDevelopment()) { var hangfireSettings = app.Services.GetRequiredService<IOptions<HangfireSettings>>().Value; app.UseHangfireDashboard(hangfireSettings.DashboardPath ?? "/hangfire", new DashboardOptions { Authorization = new[] { new HangfireAuthorizationFilter() } }); } // ...existing code... app.Run(); ### 1.3 Build and Test Backend Locally cd PetelApp.Api # Restore dependencies dotnet restore # Build in Release mode dotnet build -c Release # Test the build dotnet publish -c Release -o ./publish --no-build # Verify publish output ls ./publish # Should see: PetelApp.Api.dll, appsettings.json, web.config, etc. --- ## Step 2: Run EF Core Migrations on Azure Database CRITICAL: Initialize database schema before deploying app. ### 2.1 Set Connection String for Migrations # Windows PowerShell $env:ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection="Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" # OR Linux/Mac export ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection="Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YourSecurePassword123!;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" ### 2.2 Apply Migrations cd PetelApp.Api # List existing migrations dotnet ef migrations list --context AppDbContext # Apply migrations to Azure database dotnet ef database update --context AppDbContext # Expected output: # Applying migration '20250120_InitialCreate' # Applying migration '20250120_AddHangfireTables' # Done. ### 2.3 Verify Database Schema -- Connect to Azure PostgreSQL psql "host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com dbname=petelappdb user=PetelAdmin sslmode=require" -- List schemas \dn -- Expected: -- Name | Owner -- --------------+------------ -- hangfire | PetelAdmin -- petel_schema | PetelAdmin -- public | postgres -- List application tables \dt petel_schema. -- Expected: users, entities, schools, students, school_years, documents, etc. -- List Hangfire tables \dt hangfire. -- Expected: job, jobqueue, state, server, etc. -- Exit \q --- ## Step 3: Prepare Frontend for Deployment ### 3.1 Create Test Environment Configuration window.ENV_CONFIG = { API_BASE_URL: '/api', // ✅ Relative path - same domain as backend ENVIRONMENT: 'test', APP_URL: 'https://petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net' }; ### 3.2 Verify No Hardcoded URLs Check all JavaScript files: cd petelapp-frontend # Search for hardcoded localhost URLs (should return nothing) grep -r "localhost:5082" public/.js grep -r "localhost:3000" public/.js # ✅ All API calls should use AppConfig.getApiUrl() grep -r "AppConfig.getApiUrl" public/.js Common files to check: - config.js - Should use ENV_CONFIG.API_BASE_URL - session-manager.js - Should use AppConfig.getApiUrl() - All page scripts - Should use AppConfig.getApiUrl() ### 3.3 Update index.html for Production Verify script load order: <head> <!-- ✅ CRITICAL: Load environment config FIRST --> <script src="env-config.js"></script> <!-- Then other scripts --> <script src="config.js"></script> <script src="session-manager.js"></script> <script src="page-lifecycle-manager.js"></script> <!-- ... --> </head> --- ## Step 4: Deploy Backend to Azure ### 4.1 Create Deployment Package cd PetelApp.Api # Clean previous builds dotnet clean # Publish in Release mode dotnet publish -c Release -o ./publish # Copy frontend files to wwwroot mkdir -p ./publish/wwwroot cp -r ../petelapp-frontend/public/ ./publish/wwwroot/ # ✅ CRITICAL: Copy TEST environment config cp ../petelapp-frontend/public/env-config.test.js ./publish/wwwroot/env-config.js # Create deployment ZIP cd publish tar -czf ../deploy-test.tar.gz . # OR on Windows with 7-Zip: # 7z a -tzip ../deploy-test.zip cd .. ### 4.2 Deploy to Azure App Service # Set variables RESOURCE_GROUP="petel-test-rg" WEB_APP_NAME="petel-test-api" # Deploy ZIP package az webapp deployment source config-zip \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --name $WEB_APP_NAME \ --src deploy-test.tar.gz # Expected output: # Getting scm site credentials for zip deployment # Starting zip deployment... # Deployment endpoint responded with status code 202 # Polling deployment status... # { # "active": true, # "author": "admin", # "complete": true, # "status": 4, # "status_text": "Success" # } ### 4.3 Set Environment Variables # Set ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT to Test az webapp config appsettings set \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --name $WEB_APP_NAME \ --settings \ ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT="Test" \ WEBSITE_TIME_ZONE="Israel Standard Time" \ Database__SchemaName="petel_schema" \ Hangfire__StorageSchema="hangfire" \ Hangfire__DashboardEnabled="true" \ Hangfire__WorkerCount="1" ### 4.4 Set Connection Strings (Securely) # ✅ Set connection strings via Azure CLI (NOT in source control) DB_PASSWORD="YourSecurePassword123!" az webapp config connection-string set \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --name $WEB_APP_NAME \ --connection-string-type PostgreSQL \ --settings \ DefaultConnection="Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=$DB_PASSWORD;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" \ HangfireConnection="Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=$DB_PASSWORD;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true" ### 4.5 Restart App Service # Restart to apply configuration changes az webapp restart \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --name $WEB_APP_NAME echo "✅ Backend deployed and restarted" echo "🌐 App URL: https://$WEB_APP_NAME.azurewebsites.net" --- ## Step 5: Verify Deployment ### 5.1 Check App Service Logs # Stream live logs az webapp log tail \ --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP \ --name $WEB_APP_NAME # Look for: # ✅ "Now listening on: http://[::]:8080" # ✅ "Hangfire SQL objects installed" # ✅ "Application started" # ❌ Any exceptions or errors ### 5.2 Test Health Endpoint # Test API health curl https://petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net/api/health # Expected: 200 OK with response body ### 5.3 Test Frontend Open in browser: https://petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net Expected: - ✅ Login page loads - ✅ Hebrew RTL text displays correctly - ✅ No console errors (F12 Developer Tools) - ✅ window.AppConfig.apiBaseUrl = "/api" (check in console) ### 5.4 Test Login Flow Test with existing user (if seeded): 1. Enter username/password 2. Click login 3. Should redirect to main dashboard 4. Check browser network tab (F12): - POST /api/auth/login → 200 OK - GET /api/session → 200 OK with session data - GET /api/systemAttributes → 200 OK ### 5.5 Verify Hangfire Dashboard https://petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net/hangfire Expected: - ✅ Dashboard loads - ✅ "Servers" tab shows 1 active server - ✅ "Recurring Jobs" tab shows system attribute loader (if configured) - ✅ No failed jobs ### 5.6 Check Database Connections -- Connect to Azure PostgreSQL psql "host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com dbname=petelappdb user=PetelAdmin sslmode=require" -- Check Hangfire server is active SELECT FROM hangfire.server WHERE lastheartbeat > NOW() - INTERVAL '5 minutes'; -- Expected: 1 row with server name matching App Service instance -- Check application tables SELECT COUNT() FROM petel_schema.users; SELECT COUNT() FROM petel_schema.entities; -- Exit \q --- ## Step 6: Initial Data Setup (If Needed) ### 6.1 Seed System Attributes If SystemAttributes table is empty: # Option 1: Via SQL script psql "host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com dbname=petelappdb user=PetelAdmin sslmode=require" \ -f seed-system-attributes.sql # Option 2: Via API endpoint (if you created one) curl -X POST https://petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net/api/admin/seed-data \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" ### 6.2 Create Test User -- Connect to database psql "host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com dbname=petelappdb user=PetelAdmin sslmode=require" -- Create test user (adjust for your schema) INSERT INTO petel_schema.users (username, password_hash, full_name, entity_id, is_active) VALUES ( 'testuser', '$2a$11$...', -- Use BCrypt hash of password 'משתמש בדיקה', 1, -- Your test entity ID true ); -- Verify SELECT FROM petel_schema.users WHERE username = 'testuser'; \q --- ## Step 7: Troubleshooting Common Issues ### Issue: "Application Error" on homepage Check logs: az webapp log tail --resource-group petel-test-rg --name petel-test-api Common causes: - ❌ Connection string not set correctly - ❌ Database migrations not applied - ❌ ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT not set to "Test" Fix: # Verify connection strings az webapp config connection-string list \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --name petel-test-api # Verify app settings az webapp config appsettings list \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --name petel-test-api ### Issue: API calls return 404 Symptoms: - Frontend loads but API calls fail - Browser console shows GET /api/... 404 Not Found Causes: - ❌ Backend not properly deployed - ❌ API routes not registered in Program.cs Fix: # Check if backend DLL exists az webapp ssh --resource-group petel-test-rg --name petel-test-api # In SSH session: ls /home/site/wwwroot/ # Should see: PetelApp.Api.dll # Check if API is running curl http://localhost:8080/api/health ### Issue: Login fails with CORS error Symptoms: - Browser console: Access to fetch at '...' has been blocked by CORS policy - Login button doesn't work Cause: - ❌ CORS not configured for frontend origin Fix: # Update CORS allowed origins az webapp config appsettings set \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --name petel-test-api \ --settings Cors__AllowedOrigins__0="https://petel-test-api.azurewebsites.net" # Restart app az webapp restart --resource-group petel-test-rg --name petel-test-api ### Issue: Database connection fails Symptoms: - Logs show: Failed to connect to PostgreSQL - Npgsql.NpgsqlException: Connection refused Causes: - ❌ Firewall not allowing App Service IPs - ❌ Wrong connection string Fix: # Get App Service outbound IPs az webapp show \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --name petel-test-api \ --query "outboundIpAddresses" -o tsv # Add firewall rule for each IP az postgres flexible-server firewall-rule create \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --name petel-test-db \ --rule-name "AllowAppService" \ --start-ip-address <first-ip> \ --end-ip-address <first-ip> ### Issue: Hangfire not starting Symptoms: - /hangfire returns 404 - No active servers in Hangfire dashboard Cause: - ❌ Hangfire schema not created - ❌ HangfireConnection string incorrect Fix: # Verify Hangfire schema exists psql "host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com dbname=petelappdb user=PetelAdmin" \ -c "\dn hangfire" # If not exists, create it psql "host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com dbname=petelappdb user=PetelAdmin" \ -c "CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS hangfire; GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA hangfire TO PetelAdmin;" # Restart app to trigger Hangfire initialization az webapp restart --resource-group petel-test-rg --name petel-test-api --- ## Step 8: Post-Deployment Configuration ### 8.1 Configure Custom Domain (Optional) # Add custom domain az webapp config hostname add \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --webapp-name petel-test-api \ --hostname test.petel-system.co.il # Enable HTTPS az webapp config ssl bind \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --name petel-test-api \ --certificate-thumbprint <thumbprint> \ --ssl-type SNI ### 8.2 Enable Application Insights (Optional) # Create Application Insights az monitor app-insights component create \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --app petel-test-insights \ --location westeurope \ --application-type web # Get instrumentation key INSTRUMENTATION_KEY=$(az monitor app-insights component show \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --app petel-test-insights \ --query "instrumentationKey" -o tsv) # Configure App Service az webapp config appsettings set \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --name petel-test-api \ --settings \ APPINSIGHTS_INSTRUMENTATIONKEY="$INSTRUMENTATION_KEY" \ ApplicationInsights__InstrumentationKey="$INSTRUMENTATION_KEY" ### 8.3 Configure Backup (Recommended) # Create storage account for backups az storage account create \ --name peteltestbackups \ --resource-group petel-test-rg \ --location westeurope \ --sku Standard_LRS # Enable automated backups (requires Standard tier or higher) # Note: Basic B1 tier doesn't support automated backups # Consider upgrading to S1 for production --- ## Step 9: Create Deployment Script for Future Updates ### 9.1 Create Automated Deployment Script #!/bin/bash # filepath: deploy-test.sh set -e # Exit on error echo "🚀 Deploying Petel App to TEST environment..." # Configuration RESOURCE_GROUP="petel-test-rg" WEB_APP_NAME="petel-test-api" DB_PASSWORD="YourSecurePassword123!" # content.copilot: # Azure Deployment Error - Path Separator Issue (Windows → Linux) ## Problem Analysis The error shows backslash path separators (\) in file paths on Linux filesystem: /home/site/wwwroot/wwwroot\Plus icon.png ❌ WRONG - backslash on Linux /home/site/wwwroot/wwwroot\index.html ❌ WRONG - backslash on Linux Root Cause: Your ZIP archive was created on Windows and contains Windows-style paths with backslashes instead of Linux-style paths with forward slashes. ## Solution: Fix ZIP Creation on Windows ### Option 1: Use PowerShell with Unix-Style Paths (Recommended) # Navigate to publish folder Set-Location -Path ".\publish" Write-Host "📦 Creating deployment package with Unix-style paths..." -ForegroundColor Cyan # Remove existing package $deploymentPackage = "..\deploy-test.zip" if (Test-Path $deploymentPackage) { Remove-Item $deploymentPackage -Force } # ✅ Use tar (available in Windows 10+) for Unix-compatible paths # tar creates ZIP with forward slashes automatically tar -czf ..\deploy-test.tar.gz # OR use 7-Zip with forward slash option # 7z a -tzip ..\deploy-test.zip -x!.pdb # Return to parent directory Set-Location -Path ".." Write-Host "✅ Deployment package created with Unix paths" -ForegroundColor Green ### Option 2: Use WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) # From WSL terminal cd /mnt/c/dev/PetelFullApp/PetelApp.Api/publish # Create tar.gz with Unix paths tar -czf ../deploy-test.tar.gz . # Verify paths in archive tar -tzf ../deploy-test.tar.gz | head -20 # Should show: wwwroot/index.html (forward slashes) ### Option 3: Use Git Bash # From Git Bash terminal cd /c/dev/PetelFullApp/PetelApp.Api/publish # Create tar archive tar -czf ../deploy-test.tar.gz . cd .. ## Complete Fixed Deployment Script # Navigate to project root Set-Location -Path "c:\dev\PetelFullApp" Write-Host "🚀 Starting deployment package creation..." -ForegroundColor Cyan # 1. Navigate to backend Set-Location -Path "PetelApp.Api" # 2. Clean previous builds Write-Host "🧹 Cleaning previous builds..." -ForegroundColor Yellow dotnet clean # 3. Publish backend in Release mode Write-Host "📦 Publishing backend..." -ForegroundColor Cyan dotnet publish -c Release -o .\publish # 4. Create wwwroot directory $wwwrootPath = ".\publish\wwwroot" if (-not (Test-Path $wwwrootPath)) { New-Item -Path $wwwrootPath -ItemType Directory -Force | Out-Null } # 5. Copy frontend files to wwwroot Write-Host "📄 Copying frontend files..." -ForegroundColor Cyan Copy-Item -Path "..\petelapp-frontend\public\" -Destination $wwwrootPath -Recurse -Force # 6. ✅ Copy TEST environment config Write-Host "⚙️ Copying TEST environment configuration..." -ForegroundColor Cyan Copy-Item -Path "..\petelapp-frontend\public\env-test-config.js" -Destination "$wwwrootPath\env-config.js" -Force # 7. Verify package structure Write-Host "n📋 Verifying package structure..." -ForegroundColor Cyan $checks = @{ "Backend DLL" = Test-Path ".\publish\PetelApp.Api.dll" "appsettings.json" = Test-Path ".\publish\appsettings.json" "index.html" = Test-Path "$wwwrootPath\index.html" "env-config.js" = Test-Path "$wwwrootPath\env-config.js" "config.js" = Test-Path "$wwwrootPath\config.js" } $allPassed = $true foreach ($check in $checks.GetEnumerator()) { $status = if ($check.Value) { "✅" } else { "❌"; $allPassed = $false } $color = if ($check.Value) { "Green" } else { "Red" } Write-Host " $($check.Key): $status" -ForegroundColor $color } if (-not $allPassed) { Write-Host "n❌ Package structure verification failed!" -ForegroundColor Red exit 1 } # 8. ✅ Create deployment package using tar (Unix-compatible paths) Write-Host "n📦 Creating deployment package with Unix-style paths..." -ForegroundColor Cyan Set-Location -Path ".\publish" $deploymentPackage = "..\deploy-test.tar.gz" if (Test-Path $deploymentPackage) { Remove-Item $deploymentPackage -Force } # Use tar (available in Windows 10+ / PowerShell 5.1+) # This creates Unix-style paths automatically & tar.exe -czf $deploymentPackage if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Host "❌ tar command failed. Trying alternative method..." -ForegroundColor Red # Fallback: Use Compress-Archive but this may still have path issues # Better to install WSL or use Git Bash Set-Location -Path ".." Write-Host "⚠️ PowerShell Compress-Archive may cause path issues on Linux." -ForegroundColor Yellow Write-Host " Recommended: Use WSL, Git Bash, or install tar.exe" -ForegroundColor Yellow Compress-Archive -Path ".\publish\" -DestinationPath ".\deploy-test.zip" -Force $deploymentPackage = ".\deploy-test.zip" } else { Set-Location -Path ".." } # 9. Verify package was created if (Test-Path $deploymentPackage) { $packageSize = (Get-Item $deploymentPackage).Length / 1MB Write-Host "✅ Deployment package created successfully" -ForegroundColor Green Write-Host "📊 Package size: $([Math]::Round($packageSize, 2)) MB" -ForegroundColor Green Write-Host "📦 Package location: $(Resolve-Path $deploymentPackage)" -ForegroundColor Cyan } else { Write-Host "❌ Failed to create deployment package" -ForegroundColor Red exit 1 } Write-Host "n✅ Package ready for Azure deployment!" -ForegroundColor Green Write-Host "Next: Upload via Azure Portal → Deployment Center → ZIP Deploy" -ForegroundColor Yellow ## If tar.exe Not Available in PowerShell ### Install tar.exe (Windows 10+) tar is included in Windows 10 build 17063+. Check if you have it: # Check tar availability where.exe tar # If not found, check Windows version winver # Windows 10 1803+ includes tar natively # If older, install Git for Windows or WSL ### Alternative: Use 7-Zip with Unix Paths # Install 7-Zip from https://www.7-zip.org/ # Create ZIP with Unix paths cd .\publish & "C:\Program Files\7-Zip\7z.exe" a -tzip ..\deploy-test.zip -x!.pdb cd .. ## Deploy via Azure Portal (After Fixing ZIP) 1. Delete old deployment: - Azure Portal → App Service → Deployment Center - Stop the app service first - Advanced Tools → Go → Debug Console → CMD - Navigate to /home/site/wwwroot - Delete all files: rm -rf * 2. Upload new package: - Deployment Center → ZIP Deploy - Upload deploy-test.tar.gz (created with tar) - Wait for deployment to complete ## Verify Deployment After Upload # Via Azure Portal → Advanced Tools (Kudu) → Debug Console # Check paths use forward slashes ls -la /home/site/wwwroot/wwwroot/ # Should show: # /home/site/wwwroot/wwwroot/index.html ✅ Forward slash # /home/site/wwwroot/wwwroot/config.js ✅ Forward slash # /home/site/wwwroot/wwwroot/Plus icon.png ✅ Forward slash (with space) # NOT: # /home/site/wwwroot/wwwroot\index.html ❌ Backslash (WRONG) ## Alternative: Deploy via FTP (Avoids Path Issues) # Get FTP credentials from Azure Portal # App Service → Deployment Center → FTPS credentials # Use FileZilla or WinSCP # Connect to FTPS endpoint # Upload contents of .\publish\ to /site/wwwroot/ # Preserves correct path separators ## Fix env-config.js Path Your shows the correct URL but may need verification: window.ENV_CONFIG = { API_BASE_URL: 'https://petel-test-api-ahafcqfnh6drcdbd.israelcentral-01.azurewebsites.net/api', ENVIRONMENT: 'test' }; Verify this matches your actual App Service URL: # Get actual App Service URL az webapp show --resource-group petel-test-rg --name petel-test-api --query "defaultHostName" -o tsv # Output should match: petel-test-api-ahafcqfnh6drcdbd.israelcentral-01.azurewebsites.net ## Summary - Action Plan 1. ✅ Delete existing deployment from Azure (via Kudu console) 2. ✅ Recreate package using tar (not Compress-Archive) 3. ✅ Upload via Azure Portal → ZIP Deploy 4. ✅ Verify paths use forward slashes in Kudu console 5. ✅ Restart App Service 6. ✅ Test application in browser Key Point: The issue is Windows path separators in ZIP archive, not your application code. Using tar instead of PowerShell's Compress-Archive` will fix this.

content.copilot: # Hangfire Database Already Exists - Resolution The error indicates that Hangfire's SQL objects already exist in your PostgreSQL database. This is NOT a critical error - it just means Hangfire is attempting to create tables/schema that already exist from a previous deployment. ## Immediate Actions ### 1. Check if App is Actually Running Despite the Hangfire message, the app may be running. Test these URLs: # Test in browser or PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://petel-test-api-ahafcqfnh6drcdbd.israelcentral-01.azurewebsites.net" -UseBasicParsing Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://petel-test-api-ahafcqfnh6drcdbd.israelcentral-01.azurewebsites.net/api/health" -UseBasicParsing If these return 200 OK: Your app is running fine, Hangfire warning is harmless. ### 2. Verify Hangfire Configuration Check your appsettings.json has Hangfire settings: { "Hangfire": { "StorageSchema": "hangfire", "DashboardEnabled": true, "WorkerCount": 1 } } Check Azure App Service Configuration: 1. Azure Portal → App Service → Configuration → Application settings 2. Verify these exist: Hangfire__StorageSchema = hangfire Hangfire__DashboardEnabled = true Hangfire__WorkerCount = 1 ### 3. Fix Hangfire Initialization (If Needed) Update Program.cs to handle existing schema gracefully: // ...existing code... // ✅ Hangfire configuration with idempotent schema creation var hangfireConnectionString = builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("HangfireConnection") ?? builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection"); var hangfireSchema = builder.Configuration["Hangfire:StorageSchema"] ?? "hangfire"; builder.Services.AddHangfire(configuration => configuration .SetDataCompatibilityLevel(CompatibilityLevel.Version_180) .UseSimpleAssemblyNameTypeSerializer() .UseRecommendedSerializerSettings() .UsePostgreSqlStorage(options => { options.UseNpgsqlConnection(hangfireConnectionString); }, new PostgreSqlStorageOptions { SchemaName = hangfireSchema, PrepareSchemaIfNecessary = true, // ✅ Safe - only creates if missing EnableTransactionScopeEnlistment = true, InvisibilityTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(30) })); builder.Services.AddHangfireServer(options => { options.WorkerCount = builder.Configuration.GetValue<int>("Hangfire:WorkerCount", 1); options.ServerName = $"{Environment.MachineName}:{Guid.NewGuid()}"; }); // ...existing code... var app = builder.Build(); // ...existing code... // ✅ Hangfire Dashboard (conditional based on configuration) if (builder.Configuration.GetValue<bool>("Hangfire:DashboardEnabled", true)) { app.UseHangfireDashboard("/hangfire", new DashboardOptions { Authorization = new[] { new HangfireAuthorizationFilter() }, DashboardTitle = "Petel System - Background Jobs" }); } app.UseHangfireServer(); // ...existing code... ### 4. Clear Hangfire Schema (Nuclear Option) Only if app is NOT working and you need fresh start: -- Connect to PostgreSQL via Azure Portal Query Editor or pgAdmin -- ⚠️ WARNING: This deletes all background job history -- Drop Hangfire schema DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS hangfire CASCADE; -- Hangfire will recreate on next startup After dropping schema: 1. Restart App Service 2. Check Log Stream for successful schema creation 3. Verify Hangfire dashboard loads: /hangfire ## Understanding the Error What happened: - PrepareSchemaIfNecessary = true tells Hangfire to create tables if they don't exist - On subsequent deployments, tables already exist - Hangfire logs this as [ERR] but it's actually non-fatal - App continues to start normally after this message Why it appears as error: - Hangfire's schema creation is idempotent (safe to run multiple times) - The library logs duplicate creation attempts as errors - This is a logging issue, not an application issue ## Expected Log Output (Successful Startup) 2025-11-20T18:56:48 [INF] Starting Hangfire Server... 2025-11-20T18:56:48 [ERR] Error while executing install/upgrade The database for hangfire already exists... 2025-11-20T18:56:48 [INF] Hangfire Server started 2025-11-20T18:56:49 [INF] Now listening on: http://[::]:8080 2025-11-20T18:56:49 [INF] Application started. content.human: My zip does not have a nested wwwroot. Azure deployed all files to wwwroot, meaning that the dll files etc are under site/wwwroot and the html/js files are under site/wwwroot/wwwroot. Should the dlls be under the site folder? Meaning all files should be move up on level
content.copilot: # Azure App Service File Structure Issue You're correct! The issue is that Azure extracted your ZIP to /site/wwwroot/, but your backend DLLs need to be at the root of /site/wwwroot/, not nested. ## Correct Azure Structure /site/wwwroot/ ← App Service root ├── PetelApp.Api.dll ✅ Backend DLL at root ├── appsettings.json ✅ Config at root ├── web.config ✅ IIS config at root └── wwwroot/ ✅ Static files folder ├── index.html ✅ Frontend files ├── env-config.js ├── config.js └── login.html ## What Happened Your deployment ZIP structure is correct, but Azure ZIP Deploy extracts to /site/wwwroot/ automatically: Your ZIP: ├── PetelApp.Api.dll ├── appsettings.json └── wwwroot/ └── index.html Azure extracts to: /site/wwwroot/PetelApp.Api.dll ✅ CORRECT /site/wwwroot/appsettings.json ✅ CORRECT /site/wwwroot/wwwroot/index.html ✅ CORRECT This is actually correct! Azure knows to look for the DLL at /site/wwwroot/PetelApp.Api.dll. ## Why You're Getting 404 The 404 is because ASP.NET Core's static file middleware looks for files in the wwwroot subfolder relative to the application root. ASP.NET Core structure: Application Root: /site/wwwroot/ Static Files Root: /site/wwwroot/wwwroot/ ← Correct! When you request https://your-app.azurewebsites.net/, ASP.NET Core looks for: - /site/wwwroot/wwwroot/index.html ✅ This is correct ## Verify Current Structure Check via Kudu Console: cd /site/wwwroot ls -la # Should show: # PetelApp.Api.dll ✅ Backend at root # appsettings.json ✅ Config at root # wwwroot/ ✅ Frontend folder cd wwwroot ls -la # Should show: # index.html ✅ Frontend files # env-config.js # config.js # login.html If this structure is correct, then the 404 is caused by: ## Problem: Missing UseStaticFiles() Middleware Your Program.cs is missing the static file middleware or it's in the wrong order: csharp // ...existing code... var app = builder.Build(); // ✅ CRITICAL: Add this line BEFORE UseRouting() app.UseStaticFiles(); // Configure the HTTP request pipeline if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment()) { app.UseSwagger(); app.UseSwaggerUI(); } app.UseHttpsRedirection(); app.UseCors("AllowFrontend"); app.UseRouting(); app.UseAuthentication(); app.UseAuthorization(); // Hangfire if (builder.Configuration.GetValue<bool>("Hangfire:DashboardEnabled", true)) { app.UseHangfireDashboard("/hangfire", new DashboardOptions { Authorization = new[] { new HangfireAuthorizationFilter() }, DashboardTitle = "Petel System - Background Jobs" }); } app.UseHangfireServer(); app.MapControllers(); // ✅ CRITICAL: Add this line at the end app.MapFallbackToFile("index.html"); app.Run(); ## Fix and Redeploy 1. Update Program.cs: Add the two critical lines: - app.UseStaticFiles(); - Enables serving files from wwwroot/ - app.MapFallbackToFile("index.html"); - SPA fallback routing 2. Rebuild and Redeploy: cd c:\dev\PetelFullApp\PetelApp.Api # Clean dotnet clean Remove-Item -Path ".\publish" -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Remove-Item -Path ".\deploy-test.zip" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue # Publish dotnet publish -c Release -o .\publish # Copy frontend to wwwroot $wwwrootPath = ".\publish\wwwroot" if (Test-Path $wwwrootPath) { Remove-Item -Path $wwwrootPath -Recurse -Force } New-Item -Path $wwwrootPath -ItemType Directory -Force | Out-Null Copy-Item -Path "..\petelapp-frontend\public\" -Destination $wwwrootPath -Recurse -Force Copy-Item -Path "..\petelapp-frontend\public\env-test-config.js" -Destination "$wwwrootPath\env-config.js" -Force # Verify structure Write-Host "nVerifying structure:" Write-Host "Backend DLL: $(Test-Path '.\publish\PetelApp.Api.dll')" Write-Host "wwwroot folder: $(Test-Path $wwwrootPath)" Write-Host "index.html: $(Test-Path "$wwwrootPath\index.html")" # Create ZIP cd .\publish tar.exe -a -c -f ..\deploy-test.zip cd .. Write-Host "n✅ Package ready: deploy-test.zip" Write-Host "Upload to Azure Portal → Deployment Center → ZIP Deploy" 3. Deploy via Azure Portal: 1. Deployment Center → ZIP Deploy 2. Upload deploy-test.zip 3. Wait for deployment 4. Restart App Service 4. Test URLs: https://petel-test-api-ahafcqfnh6drcdbd.israelcentral-01.azurewebsites.net https://petel-test-api-ahafcqfnh6drcdbd.israelcentral-01.azurewebsites.net/env-config.js https://petel-test-api-ahafcqfnh6drcdbd.israelcentral-01.azurewebsites.net/api/health ## Summary DO NOT move files around in Azure - the structure is correct: - ✅ DLLs at /site/wwwroot/ (application root) - ✅ Frontend at /site/wwwroot/wwwroot/ (static files root) The fix is in Program.cs: 1. Add app.UseStaticFiles(); before app.UseRouting(); 2. Add app.MapFallbackToFile("index.html"); after app.MapControllers(); 3. Rebuild and redeploy This will enable ASP.NET Core to serve static files from the wwwroot/ subfolder correctly.

Navigate to: Azure Database for PostgreSQL → petel-test-db 2. Click "Networking" (left sidebar) 3. Click "Save" ### Step 6: Restart and Verify Restart App Service: 1. App Service → Overview 2. Click "Restart" 3. Wait 30-60 seconds Check Log Stream: 1. App Service → Log stream 2. Wait for startup messages: Expected successful startup: [INF] Starting Hangfire Server... [INF] Hangfire Server started [INF] Now listening on: http://[::]:8080 [INF] Application started If you see: ✅ Application started - SUCCESS! ### Step 7: Test Application # Test health endpoint Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://petel-test-api-ahafcqfnh6drcdbd.israelcentral-01.azurewebsites.net/api/health" -UseBasicParsing # Test frontend Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://petel-test-api-ahafcqfnh6drcdbd.israelcentral-01.azurewebsites.net" -UseBasicParsing ## Alternative: Add Connection Strings via Azure CLI # Set DefaultConnection az webapp config connection-string set --resource-group petel-test-rg --name petel-test-api --connection-string-type PostgreSQL --settings DefaultConnection="Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YOUR_PASSWORD;Port=5432;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true;" # Set HangfireConnection az webapp config connection-string set --resource-group petel-test-rg --name petel-test-api --connection-string-type PostgreSQL --settings HangfireConnection="Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com;Database=petelappdb;Username=PetelAdmin;Password=YOUR_PASSWORD;Port=5432;SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true;" # Restart app az webapp restart --resource-group petel-test-rg --name petel-test-api ## Common Connection String Issues ### Issue 1: Wrong Host ❌ Host=localhost # Wrong - dev environment ❌ Host=[::1] # Wrong - IPv6 localhost ✅ Host=petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com # Correct ### Issue 2: Missing SSL Mode ❌ Without SSL Mode # Connection refused ✅ SSL Mode=Require;Trust Server Certificate=true; # Correct ### Issue 3: Wrong Username Format ❌ Username=PetelAdmin@petel-test-db # Old format ✅ Username=PetelAdmin # Correct for Flexible Server ### Issue 4: Firewall Blocking Error: "Connection timed out" Fix: Add Azure services to PostgreSQL firewall rules ## Verification Checklist After configuration: 1. ✅ Connection strings set in Azure Portal → Configuration 2. ✅ Application settings set (ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT, Database__SchemaName, etc.) 3. ✅ PostgreSQL firewall allows Azure services 4. ✅ App service restarted after configuration changes 5. ✅ Log stream shows "Application started" without database errors 6. ✅ Health endpoint returns 200 OK 7. ✅ Frontend loads at root URL ## Debug Connection String If still failing, verify connection string is loaded: Add temporary logging to Program.cs: csharp // After builder creation, before services var connectionString = builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection"); Console.WriteLine($"🔍 Connection String: {connectionString?.Substring(0, Math.Min(50, connectionString.Length ?? 0))}..."); if (connectionString?.Contains("localhost") == true || connectionString?.Contains("[::1]") == true) { Console.WriteLine("⚠️ WARNING: Using localhost connection string in production!"); } Check Log Stream after restart to see what connection string is being used. ## Summary The issue is: App trying to connect to localhost instead of Azure PostgreSQL. HangfireConnection - Hangfire background jobs database Both should point to: petel-test-db.postgres.database.azure.com After configuration, the app will connect to Azure PostgreSQL and start successfully.

Environment-Specific Origins // appsettings.Development.json { "Cors": { "AllowedOrigins": [ "http://localhost:3000", "http://localhost:5173" ] } } // appsettings.Test.json { "Cors": { "AllowedOrigins": [ "https://test.petel.site", "https://petel-test-api-ahafcqfnh6drcdbd.israelcentral-01.azurewebsites.net" ] } } // appsettings.Production.json { "Cors": { "AllowedOrigins": [ "https://petel.site", "https://www.petel.site", "https://app.petel.site" ] } } ### 2. Dynamic Origin Validation // For multi-tenant scenarios policy.SetIsOriginAllowed(origin => { // Log for debugging Console.WriteLine($"🔍 CORS request from: {origin}"); // Check against configured list var isAllowed = corsOrigins.Contains(origin); if (!isAllowed) { Console.WriteLine($"⚠️ CORS blocked: {origin}"); } return isAllowed; }); ## Verification Checklist After configuration: 1. ✅ CORS origins added to appsettings.json or Azure settings 2. ✅ Program.cs reads configuration via GetSection("Cors:AllowedOrigins") 3. ✅ CORS middleware applied BEFORE authentication 4. ✅ AllowCredentials enabled for authentication scenarios 5. ✅ App service restarted after configuration change 6. ✅ Origin format correct (https://petel.site, no trailing slash) 7. ✅ Test from browser at https://petel.site 8. ✅ Check logs for CORS debug messages 9. ✅ Frontend env-config.js points to correct API URL 10. ✅ Both www and non-www origins included if needed ## Summary The CORS error is fixed by: 1. Restart App Service: Apply configuration changes 4. Test: Verify requests from https://petel.site succeed Recommended approach: Use application-level CORS configuration in appsettings.json` for environment-specific control, synchronized with Azure app settings. content.copilot: # Azure AD Authentication Blocking Public Access The issue is that your Azure App Service has Azure AD authentication enabled, which requires users to authenticate with Microsoft accounts before accessing the backend API. ## Problem Analysis What's Happening: - Browser with Azure AD session → Can access backend ✅ - Browser without Azure AD session → Gets 401/403 ❌ - Frontend at https://petel.site cannot access API because users aren't Azure AD authenticated This means: Azure App Service has "Easy Auth" (Azure AD) enabled, blocking all unauthenticated requests. ## Solution: Disable Azure AD Authentication (Allow Anonymous Access) Your application has its own authentication system (JWT tokens in backend), so you don't need Azure AD authentication at the App Service level. ### Step 1: Disable Azure AD Authentication Via Azure Portal: 1. Navigate to: App Services → petel-test-api-ahafcqfnh6drcdbd 2. Click "Authentication" (left sidebar under Settings) 3. Check the current status: - If it shows "App Service authentication: On" → This is the problem 4. Click "Edit" or toggle to "Off" 5. Click "Save" 6. Restart the app service Via Azure CLI: # Disable App Service authentication az webapp auth update --resource-group petel-test-rg --name petel-test-api --enabled false # Restart app service az webapp restart --resource-group petel-test-rg --name petel-test-api ### Step 2: Verify Authentication is Disabled Check via Portal: 1. App Service → Authentication 2. Should show: "App Service authentication: Off" Check via CLI: az webapp auth show --resource-group petel-test-rg --name petel-test-api --query enabled # Should return: false ### Step 3: Configure Allowed Anonymous Endpoints Ensure your backend allows anonymous access to public endpoints: csharp // ...existing code... var app = builder.Build(); // ✅ Static files (frontend) - anonymous access app.UseStaticFiles(); // ✅ System attributes - anonymous access // Already has [AllowAnonymous] in controller app.UseHttpsRedirection(); app.UseCors("AllowFrontend"); app.UseRouting(); // ✅ Authentication/Authorization middleware app.UseAuthentication(); // Validates JWT tokens app.UseAuthorization(); // Checks [Authorize] attributes // ...existing code... app.MapControllers(); app.MapFallbackToFile("index.html"); app.Run(); Verify SystemAttributesController has [AllowAnonymous]: csharp using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization; using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc; [ApiController] [Route("api/[controller]")] [AllowAnonymous] // ✅ CRITICAL - Allows access without authentication public class SystemAttributesController : ControllerBase { private readonly SystemAttributeCache _systemCache; public SystemAttributesController(SystemAttributeCache systemCache) { _systemCache = systemCache; } [HttpGet] [AllowAnonymous] // ✅ Explicit on endpoint public IActionResult GetAll() { var attributes = _systemCache.GetAllAttributes(); return Ok(attributes); } // ...other endpoints... } Verify AuthController allows login: csharp using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization; using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc; [ApiController] [Route("api/[controller]")] public class AuthController : ControllerBase { // ...existing code... [HttpPost("login")] [AllowAnonymous] // ✅ CRITICAL - Login must be accessible public async Task<IActionResult> Login([FromBody] LoginRequest request) { // Validate credentials // Return JWT token } [HttpPost("refresh")] [AllowAnonymous] // ✅ Token refresh public async Task<IActionResult> RefreshToken([FromBody] RefreshTokenRequest request) { // Refresh token logic } } ### Step 4: Test Anonymous Access After disabling Azure AD authentication: # Test from unauthenticated browser/Postman # Should return 200 OK (no Azure AD redirect) # 1. Test system attributes (public endpoint) Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://petel-test-api-ahafcqfnh6drcdbd.israelcentral-01.azurewebsites.net/api/systemattributes" -UseBasicParsing # 2. Test frontend (public static files) Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://petel-test-api-ahafcqfnh6drcdbd.israelcentral-01.azurewebsites.net" -UseBasicParsing # 3. Test login endpoint (public endpoint) $loginBody = @{ username = "testuser" password = "testpass" } | ConvertTo-Json Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://petel-test-api-ahafcqfnh6drcdbd.israelcentral-01.azurewebsites.net/api/auth/login" -Method POST -Body $loginBody -ContentType "application/json" -UseBasicParsing Expected results (all should work without Azure AD login): - System attributes → 200 OK with JSON data - Frontend → 200 OK with HTML content - Login endpoint → 200 OK with JWT token ### Step 5: Test from petel.site Open browser (without Azure session): 1. Navigate to: https://petel.site 2. Should load login page without Azure AD redirect 3. Enter credentials and login 4. Should authenticate using backend JWT (not Azure AD) ## Alternative: Keep Azure AD for Portal Access Only If you need Azure AD authentication for Azure Portal/Kudu access but want public API access: ### Configure Authentication with Exclusions Via Portal: 1. App Service → Authentication 2. Enable authentication: On 3. Click "Add identity provider" → Azure Active Directory 4. Configure provider settings 5. CRITICAL: Under "Restrict access": - Select: "Allow unauthenticated access" - This allows Azure AD for portal but not for API Add exclusion paths in web.config: xml <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?> <configuration> <system.webServer> <handlers> <add name="aspNetCore" path="" verb="" modules="AspNetCoreModuleV2" resourceType="Unspecified" /> </handlers> <aspNetCore processPath="dotnet" arguments=".\PetelApp.Api.dll" stdoutLogEnabled="false" stdoutLogFile=".\logs\stdout" hostingModel="inprocess" /> <!-- ✅ Exclude API paths from Azure AD authentication --> <location path="api"> <system.webServer> <security> <authentication> <anonymousAuthentication enabled="true" /> </authentication> </security> </system.webServer> </location> </system.webServer> </configuration> However, this approach is complex and not recommended - better to disable Azure AD entirely and use application-level authentication. ## Security Considerations After disabling Azure AD: ✅ Frontend is still protected - Login page requires credentials ✅ API endpoints are protected - [Authorize] attribute requires JWT token ✅ Session management is secure - Backend validates tokens and maintains sessions ✅ Public endpoints are intentional - Only /api/systemattributes and /api/auth/login are public What changes: - ❌ No Azure Portal-level authentication - Anyone can access Azure infrastructure endpoints (Kudu, SCM) - ✅ Application-level authentication remains - Your JWT-based auth is unaffected To protect Azure infrastructure: 1. Use IP restrictions in Azure Portal 2. Configure VNet integration for internal-only access 3. Use Azure AD for Azure Portal access (not App Service authentication) ## Common Scenarios ### Scenario 1: Development/Test Environment (Recommended) Azure AD Authentication: OFF Application Authentication: JWT tokens Public Access: Allowed (with application auth) This is what you want for petel-test-api. ### Scenario 2: Production with Public Access Azure AD Authentication: OFF Application Authentication: JWT tokens + MFA IP Restrictions: Optional (whitelist known IPs) Rate Limiting: Enabled (DDoS protection) WAF: Enabled (Azure Front Door/Application Gateway) ### Scenario 3: Internal Corporate App Azure AD Authentication: ON Application Authentication: Optional (Azure AD replaces it) Public Access: Denied (corporate network only) ## Verification Checklist After disabling Azure AD authentication: 1. ✅ Azure Portal: Authentication shows "Off" 2. ✅ Unauthenticated browser: Can access frontend at root URL 3. ✅ System attributes: /api/systemattributes returns 200 OK 4. ✅ Login endpoint: /api/auth/login accessible without Azure AD 5. ✅ Protected endpoints: /api/students returns 401 without JWT token 6. ✅ CORS working: Requests from https://petel.site succeed 7. ✅ Frontend login: Users can authenticate via application login 8. ✅ JWT auth working: Protected endpoints accessible with valid token ## Troubleshooting ### Still getting 401 after disabling Azure AD Check: 1. App service restarted after configuration change 2. Browser cache cleared (Azure AD cookies may persist) 3. Test in incognito/private browsing mode 4. Verify Authentication section shows "Off" in portal ### Getting redirect to Microsoft login Cause: Azure AD authentication still enabled Fix: # Force disable az webapp auth update --resource-group petel-test-rg --name petel-test-api --enabled false # Clear authentication settings az webapp auth config-version upgrade --resource-group petel-test-rg --name petel-test-api # Restart az webapp restart --resource-group petel-test-rg --name petel-test-api ### CORS errors persist After disabling Azure AD, CORS errors should resolve if: - Backend CORS configuration includes https://petel.site - App service restarted - No Azure AD pre-flight request blocking ## Summary The fix: 1. ✅ Disable Azure AD authentication in App Service settings 2. ✅ Restart app service 3. ✅ Test from unauthenticated browser 4. ✅ Verify application-level JWT auth still works Your application has its own robust authentication system (JWT tokens, session management, entity validation). Azure AD authentication at the App Service level is unnecessary and blocks public access to your SaaS application. After disabling Azure AD, users from https://petel.site will be able to: - Load the frontend (public static files) - Access system attributes (public endpoint) - Login via your application auth (JWT tokens) - Access protected endpoints with valid tokens The Azure AD authentication was intended for internal corporate apps, not public SaaS applications like yours.

content.copilot: The issue is that PostgreSQL can't compare character varying[] (varchar array) with text[]. EF Core's .Contains() method generates an array containment operator that requires matching types. You need to use EF.Functions.ArrayContains() or cast the comparison value. Here's the fix: `csharp using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc; using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore; using PetelApp.Api.Data; using PetelApp.Api.Session; namespace PetelApp.Api.Controllers { [ApiController] [Route("api/[controller]")] public class TracksController : BaseController { private readonly AppDbContext _context; public TracksController( AppDbContext context, UserSessionService userSessionService, ILogger<TracksController> logger) : base(userSessionService, logger) { _context = context; } [HttpGet("by-year/{yearId}")] public async Task<IActionResult> GetTracksByYear(int yearId) { try { _logger.LogInformation("Loading tracks for year {YearId}", yearId); var tracks = await _context.Tracks .AsNoTracking() .Where(t => t.YearId == yearId && t.Id >= 100000) .Select(t => new { id = t.Id, name = t.TrackName, yearId = t.YearId, externalCode = t.ExternalCode, availableForClasses = t.AvailableForClasses }) .OrderBy(t => t.name) .ToListAsync(); _logger.LogInformation("Found {Count} tracks for year {YearId}", tracks.Count, yearId); return Ok(new { success = true, data = tracks, message = "Tracks retrieved successfully" }); } catch (Exception ex) { _logger.LogError(ex, "Error getting tracks for year {YearId}", yearId); return StatusCode(500, new { success = false, message = "שגיאה בטעינת מגמות", error = ex.Message }); } } /// <summary> /// Get tracks filtered by year and class level /// Filters tracks where the class level appears in available_for_classes array /// </summary> [HttpGet("by-year/{yearId}/class-level/{classLevel}")] public async Task<IActionResult> GetTracksByYearAndClassLevel(int yearId, string classLevel) { try { _logger.LogInformation("Loading tracks for year {YearId} and class level {ClassLevel}", yearId, classLevel); // ✅ FIX: Use ANY with explicit cast to match PostgreSQL array types var tracks = await _context.Tracks .AsNoTracking() .Where(t => t.YearId == yearId && t.Id >= 100000 && (t.AvailableForClasses == null || t.AvailableForClasses.Length == 0 || t.AvailableForClasses.Any(c => c == classLevel))) .Select(t => new { id = t.Id, name = t.TrackName, yearId = t.YearId, externalCode = t.ExternalCode, availableForClasses = t.AvailableForClasses }) .OrderBy(t => t.name) .ToListAsync(); _logger.LogInformation("Found {Count} tracks for year {YearId} and class level {ClassLevel}", tracks.Count, yearId, classLevel); return Ok(new { success = true, data = tracks, message = "Tracks retrieved successfully" }); } catch (Exception ex) { _logger.LogError(ex, "Error getting tracks for year {YearId} and class level {ClassLevel}", yearId, classLevel); return StatusCode(500, new { success = false, message = "שגיאה בטעינת מגמות", error = ex.Message }); } } } } ## Alternative Approach (Client-Side Filtering) If the .Any() approach still has issues with PostgreSQL array translation, you can load all tracks and filter in memory: csharp [HttpGet("by-year/{yearId}/class-level/{classLevel}")] public async Task<IActionResult> GetTracksByYearAndClassLevel(int yearId, string classLevel) { try { _logger.LogInformation("Loading tracks for year {YearId} and class level {ClassLevel}", yearId, classLevel); // ✅ ALTERNATIVE: Load all tracks for the year, then filter in memory var allTracks = await _context.Tracks .AsNoTracking() .Where(t => t.YearId == yearId && t.Id >= 100000) .Select(t => new { id = t.Id, name = t.TrackName, yearId = t.YearId, externalCode = t.ExternalCode, availableForClasses = t.AvailableForClasses }) .ToListAsync(); // Filter in memory for array containment var tracks = allTracks .Where(t => t.availableForClasses == null || t.availableForClasses.Length == 0 || t.availableForClasses.Contains(classLevel)) .OrderBy(t => t.name) .ToList(); _logger.LogInformation("Found {Count} tracks for year {YearId} and class level {ClassLevel}", tracks.Count, yearId, classLevel); return Ok(new { success = true, data = tracks, message = "Tracks retrieved successfully" }); } catch (Exception ex) { _logger.LogError(ex, "Error getting tracks for year {YearId} and class level {ClassLevel}", yearId, classLevel); return StatusCode(500, new { success = false, message = "שגיאה בטעינת מגמות", error = ex.Message }); } } ## Summary of Changes Problem: PostgreSQL couldn't match .Contains() operator on varchar[] array - EF Core generated incompatible SQL. Solution 1 (Recommended): Changed .Contains(classLevel) to .Any(c => c == classLevel) which generates compatible SQL for PostgreSQL array queries. Solution 2 (Fallback): Load all tracks into memory first with .ToListAsync(), then filter using LINQ-to-Objects .Contains() which works with any array type. Why This Happens: - EF Core translates .Contains() on arrays to PostgreSQL's @> containment operator - This operator requires exact type matching between array types - .Any() translates to PostgreSQL's = ANY() operator which handles type coercion better - Memory filtering avoids SQL translation issues entirely The first approach (using .Any()`) is more efficient as it filters in the database. Use the second approach only if PostgreSQL array handling remains problematic.

Browser Tab: Next to the page title in the browser tab [🔷] כניסה למערכת - Login Page 2. Bookmark Bar: When users bookmark your page 3. Browser History: In the browser's history list 4. Mobile Home Screen: When users add the site to their mobile device home screen 5. Task Bar: When the browser is minimized (Windows taskbar shows the favicon) ## Purpose - Brand Identity: Helps users quickly identify your site among multiple open tabs - Professional Appearance: Makes the site look complete and polished - Navigation: Users can find your tab more easily when they have many tabs open - Bookmarking: Provides visual recognition in bookmark lists ## Common Formats - ICO: .ico - Traditional format, supports multiple sizes - PNG: .png - Modern format, better quality - SVG: .svg - Scalable vector format (best for modern browsers) ## Standard Sizes - 16×16 pixels: Minimum size for browser tabs - 32×32 pixels: Standard size for most browsers - 48×48 pixels: For high-resolution displays - 180×180 pixels: For iOS devices (Apple Touch Icon) ## Current Fix for Your Login Page html <!-- Add in <head> section --> <link rel="icon" type="image/png" href="petel_logo.png"> This uses your existing petel_logo.png as the favicon.
